title: Data Engineer III - FMX
descriptionHtml:
About Us

Fanatics is building a leading global digital sports platform. We ignite the passions of global sports fans and maximize the presence and reach for our hundreds of sports partners globally by offering products and services across Fanatics Commerce, Fanatics Collectibles, and Fanatics Betting & Gaming, allowing sports fans to Buy, Collect, and Bet. Through the Fanatics platform, sports fans can buy licensed fan gear, jerseys, lifestyle and streetwear products, headwear, and hardgoods; collect physical and digital trading cards, sports memorabilia, and other digital assets; and bet as the company builds its Sportsbook and iGaming platform. Fanatics has an established database of over 100 million global sports fans; a global partner network with approximately 900 sports properties, including major national and international professional sports leagues, players associations, teams, colleges, college conferences and retail partners, 2,500 athletes and celebrities, and 200 exclusive athletes; and over 2,000 retail locations, including its Lids retail stores. Our more than 22,000 employees are committed to relentlessly enhancing the fan experience and delighting sports fans globally.  Data Engineer III

About the Role
We're looking for a Data Engineer III to join our Data Engineering team, which builds and governs the data foundation that powers the business. You'll work within our stack — Python ingestion pipelines, Airflow orchestration, and Snowflake/Databricks — helping move data reliably and securely from source to decision-ready output.
You'll implement features and fixes against a given design, handle known classes of pipeline issues on your own, and escalate genuinely novel problems with clear context rather than working them in isolation. You're also expected to start contributing meaningfully in code review — catching real bugs, not just style nits.

What You'll Do
  • Implement new ingestion sources end-to-end against a senior engineer's design — connector code, DAG, schema, monitoring, and catalog registration — extending the team's existing framework where a new source needs a pattern it doesn't yet support
  • Investigate pipeline failures independently, recognize known classes of issues, and ship the documented fix without needing to escalate
  • Before shipping a new pipeline, identify downstream consumers and what would break if data were late or wrong, and flag gaps like this during spec review — before writing code
  • Write clear handovers when escalating a genuinely unresolved issue — what you tried, what you ruled out, and where things diverge — so a senior can pick up without re-discovery
  • Review peers' pipeline PRs and catch non-obvious issues (e.g., missing idempotency checks, race conditions) that could cause incorrect downstream data
  • Turn ambiguous "why is this data wrong?" questions into structured investigations — tracing data lineage from source to warehouse and communicating back what you found
  • Surface concerns in spec review as specific, well-reasoned questions rather than staying silent or blocking progress
  • Support data security and governance work (e.g., PII masking, access controls) and contribute to data delivery work, including reverse ETL integrations
  • Build strong working relationships with internal stakeholders and help scope and clarify requirements for new work
  • Mentor DE2s on their first significant projects — pairing on tricky decisions and helping them apply team conventions


What We're Looking For
  • 3–5 years of professional software or data engineering experience
  • Strong SQL and Python skills, with solid experience building and operating production data pipelines
  • Comfort investigating and root-causing pipeline issues independently before escalating
  • Experience with workflow orchestration tools (Airflow or similar) and a cloud data warehouse/lakehouse (Snowflake, Databricks, or similar)
  • Solid understanding of data pipeline concepts: idempotency, schema evolution, backfills, and data quality/testing
  • Experience giving substantive code review feedback, not just style or formatting comments
  • Strong communication skills — can write a clear technical handover, ask sharp questions in spec review, and explain a data lineage investigation to a non-technical stakeholder
  • A track record of taking ownership of known-class problems end-to-end rather than needing step-by-step direction

Nice to Have
  • Experience extending or building reusable pipeline frameworks/templates
  • Exposure to reverse ETL tools or patterns, PII masking, or data access governance (RBAC)
  • Exposure to observability/monitoring tooling (e.g., Datadog) for pipeline health and alerting
  • Some experience mentoring or informally supporting more junior engineers
  • Background in gaming, betting, e-commerce, or another regulated/high-compliance industry

Why Join Us
  • Real ownership over known-class problems, with senior/staff support available for the genuinely novel ones
  • Work on high-visibility, high-trust systems that the business depends on
  • A culture built around clear tenets: standardize before you scale, own the outcome (not just the ticket), and clarity over complexity
  • Clear growth path into Senior Data Engineer, with room to start mentoring and shaping team practices along the way

At Stark, we forge the future of European and national security through cutting-edge, AI-driven technology and unmatched engineering precision. As a premier defence technology company, our mission is clear: to equip NATO Allies and their partners  with next-generation autonomous defence platforms and advanced AI-driven software built to perform in the world’s most demanding environments.

We believe that true security stems from relentless innovation. By combining elite engineering talent with agile technology and an AI-native operational culture, Stark turns complex defence challenges into field-tested, multi-domain solutions.

  • The software and systems you work on directly protect personnel and defend European and national sovereignty.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Data Operations team at Stark builds and maintains the core data pipelines, sensor logging, and annotation workflows that feed our AI and perception models. Operating at the intersection of hardware testing, flight logs, and machine learning, the team ensures high-throughput, high-fidelity data availability. We work closely with ML Engineers, perception experts, and external labeling partners to scale training data for autonomous defence systems.

YOUR MISSION

You are the crucial bridge between our raw field data, our external labeling partners, and our internal Machine Learning teams. Your mission is to ensure our AI models are trained on the highest quality data possible. You will own the day-to-day operations of the data labeling lifecycle: curating raw data, preparing annotation batches, managing vendor communication, and rigorously assessing the quality of incoming labels. If you are highly organized, detail-oriented, and interested in the intersection of data operations and Computer Vision, this is the perfect place to start your career in AI.

WHAT YOU WILL DO AT STARK

  • Own the day-to-day data labeling lifecycle: curate raw field data, create annotation batches, and prepare deliveries for external labeling companies.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for external data annotation vendors, clarifying edge cases and providing feedback on labeling guidelines.
  • Conduct rigorous Quality Assurance (QA) assessments on incoming label deliveries, track error rates, and create performance reports.
  • Support data curation efforts, filtering and selecting the most valuable sensor data (images, video, lidar) for model training.
  • Work closely with ML Engineers to understand their data needs, edge cases, and specific Computer Vision requirements.
  • Help maintain the data catalog by ensuring incoming datasets are properly tagged and logged.

WHAT YOU BRING TO THE MISSION

  • Highly organized and detail-oriented: you can manage multiple data batches, vendor deliveries, and QA processes simultaneously without dropping the ball.
  • Strong communication skills: you are comfortable coordinating with external vendors and writing clear, unambiguous instructions/guidelines.
  • Basic understanding of Computer Vision and Machine Learning concepts (e.g., bounding boxes, segmentation masks, object tracking).
  • Comfortable with basic scripting (Python) and data querying (SQL) to automate small tasks or filter data batches.

descriptionHtml:
About hyperexponential (hx)

At hyperexponential, we’re building the AI-powered platform that enables the world’s most critical decisions in a $7 trillion industry - which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms.

Until now, insurers have been making billion-dollar decisions using outdated tools. We’re changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision - helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence.

Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we’re scaling globally - already trusted by nearly 50 of the world’s largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx.

What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do - from building the world’s first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates.

What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn’t tied to title or tenure; it’s defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you’ll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure.

If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next.

About the Delivery Engineering team

The hyperexponential Delivery Engineering team is a unique blend of engineers, actuaries, mathematicians and data scientists. We don’t take on traditional “transformations” (we have brilliant partners for that) – we specialise in handling only the most difficult and interesting problems our customers face, where only a combination of technical depth, market expertise and hx knowledge will do.

The Delivery Engineering team are the experts' experts of the hx platform, knowing it top-to-bottom, inside-out – both breadth and depth. You’ll learn its limits and which can be pushed. Required Qualifications

Preferred Qualifications

title: Director Go-to-Market and Revenue Strategy
descriptionHtml:
Who We Are

You've ordered dinner through Just Eat Takeaway. You've bought and sold on OLX. You've paid with PayU. Chances are, you've already used a Prosus company today.

We are Prosus, a global technology company powering some of the world's leading lifestyle ecommerce businesses. Every day, billions of people across India, Latin America, Europe and beyond use our products and services to buy, sell, pay, connect and discover.

Our AI-driven ecosystem spans 100+ companies across ecommerce, food delivery, fintech and experiences, serving billions of consumers worldwide. AI powers how we operate and innovate, with more than 60,000 active AI agents helping our teams build, scale and move faster. Through our investment team, we also back the founders and technologies shaping the future: From robotics and autonomous systems to synthetic biology and frontier AI.

Guided by our five values Innovation, Results, People, Impact, and Entrepreneurship, culture is our competitive advantage. We thrive with experimentation; we build, we test, we learn, we iterate.

Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale.

WHO YOU ARE

You are a commercial leader who has built the go-to-market of a platform from a blank page and knows what it takes to turn a product that people already use into a business that pays for itself. You have priced and packaged products for marketplaces, brands or merchants, and you have seen the difference between a model that looks good in a spreadsheet and one that a small business owner actually adopts.

You are comfortable in a B2B2C world: the customer is reached through someone else's channel, the data belongs to the ecosystem, and the money comes from several ends of a transaction at once. You influence without authority, because the teams that execute will rarely report to you. You are rigorous with numbers and plain with people, and you are at ease saying what the evidence shows even when the room expects something else.

You want to build something that reaches millions of small businesses, you are prepared to work for it.

THE OPPORTUNITY

Toqan for Partners is the AI assistant for the merchants across the companies of the Prosus ecosystem: restaurants, pharmacies, hotels, sellers, real estate agencies and car dealers, five million businesses in total. It launched to restaurants on iFood in Brazil in September 2026 and reached 65,000 restaurants in four weeks with no media spend.

The next twelve months decide how it will become a business: which applications partners pay for and at what price, how value is shared with everyone the partner transacts with, how the uplift is measured and published so the next company embeds, and how the product travels from iFood to the rest of the ecosystem and to India and Europe. You will lead that work, as the owner of the go-to-market and the revenue strategy of Toqan for Partners, alongside the product and technology leads who own what gets built.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

Own the commercial model

Define pricing and packaging for the applications partners pay for, media management, supply, finance and operations, at a fraction of what they spend today and justified by the return they see. Design how Toqan takes part in the value it creates for the other end: take rate on agent-negotiated supply, credit origination, brand and industry media, and cross-sell of the ecosystem companies' own products. Set the rules that keep it honest, starting with the separation between paid placement and recommendation.

Drive the rollout across the ecosystem

With the Head of Operations, secure the commitment of each business in the ecosystem: sponsor, distribution, conditional yes and first market. Run the rollout inside each one, working through the teams that own the merchant relationship, and bring the product to its next verticals and markets.

Build the measurement

Own the scoreboard: active partners under a strict definition, uplift per business in retention and GMV, cost and value per active partner. Make the uplift the argument that brings the next company in and the evidence behind every pricing decision.

Structure the partnerships that carry the revenue

Lead the commercial agreements with distributors, industry, fintechs and the ecosystem companies' commercial platforms, from first conversation to signed terms, and the co-investment models that align their incentives with the partner's.

Build and lead the team

Hire and develop a small go-to-market and revenue team, growth on the merchant side, monetisation and analytics, and set its standard for rigour, ownership and candour.

WHAT YOU BRING

  • Ten or more years in go-to-market, revenue or commercial strategy, with at least one commercial function built from scratch and grown to scale.

  • Hands-on experience with pricing and packaging, ideally for marketplaces, retail media, payments or SaaS sold to small businesses.

  • Experience on more than one side of a marketplace: merchants or sellers, brands or suppliers, the platform itself.

  • A track record of adoption at scale with a long tail of small customers, not only of large enterprise deals.

  • Proven ability to move a result through teams that do not report to you, and to work inside another company's channel.

  • Fluency with data: you build the business case, run the analysis and read the uplift yourself, and use AI tooling as a normal part of how you work.

  • Candour, humility and patience: you say what the numbers say, you arrive to learn before you teach.

  • English required; Portuguese or Spanish strongly preferred.

WHAT WE OFFER

  • Global impact: a product that reaches five million small businesses across Latin America, Europe and India.

  • Ownership: the commercial model of a new business, with the numbers to be judged on and the autonomy to build it.

  • Growth: exposure to the leadership of the group and of its companies, and a clear path into operating roles in the ecosystem.

  • Competitive compensation and the Prosus benefits package for the location of the role.

Why Prosus?

At Prosus, your colleagues include 60,000 AI agents… and your job is to figure out what that actually means. We're one of the largest operators of agentic AI on the planet, inside a $100B+ portfolio across 100+ companies and two billion people. The humans here own what AI can't do alone: judgment, creativity, and the call on what gets built next.

Own the impact. Work the ecosystem. Earn your growth. Build with backing.

Curious about our perks and benefits? Take a look at this page.

Our Diversity & Inclusion Commitment

We respect the dignity and human rights of individuals and communities wherever we operate in the world. Building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels welcome and can thrive is critical for us. title: Director, Partnerships
descriptionHtml:
About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Ramp is building it's UK business from the ground up. We are looking for a Director of Partnerships to be the senior commercial owner of Ramp’s partner ecosystem in the UK: creating the relationships, market presence, and repeatable routes to revenue that help make Ramp a category-defining company in the region.

Reporting to the VP of Channel Sales, you will operate as a founder for Partnerships in London. You will build a focused partner strategy, develop executive-level relationships, and turn the right relationships into durable commercial outcomes. You will work closely with the UK go-to-market team and cross-functional leaders across Sales, Product, Marketing, and Customer Success to make partnerships a meaningful driver of market entry and long-term growth.

This is not a role for someone looking to inherit a mature playbook. The right person is entrepreneurial, commercially sharp, and comfortable creating clarity where there is none. They can move from a first meeting with a senior executive to a clear point of view, an internal plan, and disciplined follow-through.

What You'll Do

  • Own and execute Ramp’s UK partnerships strategy, identifying the partner categories and individual relationships that can accelerate awareness, pipeline, customer value, and long-term market position

  • Build and maintain senior relationships across the UK ecosystem, including accounting, private equity and venture capital firms, professional-services and consulting firms, financial institutions, technology partners, and other high-leverage channels

  • Work alongside the UK Channel Partner Managers, aligning the broader ecosystem strategy with Ramp’s dedicated motions and creating leverage across shared relationships

  • Develop a focused partnership plan for priority relationships: articulate the joint value proposition, define the commercial path, and create mutual accountability for progress

  • Generate measurable commercial impact by sourcing and influencing pipeline, creating warm paths to target customers, and supporting strategic deals through partner relationships

  • Represent Ramp with credibility at executive meetings, industry events, and partner forums, building the company’s reputation as a serious, long-term UK partner

  • Serve as the internal voice of the UK partner market, translating relationship intelligence, customer needs, and market dynamics into actionable input for Sales, Product, Marketing, and leadership

  • Build the operating cadence for the function, including account plans, partnership scorecards, executive briefs, pipeline visibility, and clear follow-through across internal and external stakeholders

  • Help shape Ramp’s broader UK and European go-to-market strategy as the market, team, and partnership portfolio grow

What You Need

  • 10+ years of experience in sales, partnerships, business development, alliances, or go-to-market leadership, with a demonstrated record of building senior relationships and driving commercial outcomes

  • A proven track record of owning revenue, quota, influenced pipeline, or similarly concrete commercial goals in a complex B2B environment

  • Executive presence and sound judgment: you can earn credibility with senior partner leaders and represent Ramp confidently in consequential conversations

  • A builder mindset. You have launched a territory, vertical, business line, or partner motion, and know how to create a plan and operating rhythm from a blank page

  • The ability to turn broad relationships into specific opportunities, navigate multiple stakeholders, and maintain momentum through long sales and partnership cycles

  • Strong strategic and analytical thinking, with the ability to decide where Ramp should invest and make a clear, data-informed case to senior leadership

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to build a compelling partnership narrative and align cross-functional teams around it

  • AI fluency as a daily habit. Ramp is a builder culture: if you do not instinctively reach for AI before doing things manually, this role will be a hard adjustment

  • Ability to work five days per week from Ramp’s London office, with willingness to travel across the UK and continental Europe as needed

Nice to Haves

  • Experience selling or partnering into private equity, financial services, consulting, enterprise technology, or high-growth software companies

  • Experience in fintech, financial software, payments, spend management, or the office of the CFO technology ecosystem

  • An established UK network of senior commercial, investment, operating, or technology leaders

  • Experience building a new market or international go-to-market motion

  • Fluency in an additional European language

Why Ramp

We're building a sales team that wins, and we're looking for the leaders who'll make it happen.

As Director Sales at Lio, you're a true player-coach. You build, coach and lead a team of 6–8 Account Executives, and when a big deal is on the line, you're right there in the room helping close it. You don't chase a quota of your own. You own your team's number, and the goal is ambitious: hit the target together, then double it.


What you'll do

  • Lead your team to its number. You help your team hit its target and build the pipeline and habits that let it grow from there.

  • Be there when deals need you. You join calls, visit customers on site and help close seven-figure opportunities. When the usual playbook isn't enough, you get creative.

  • Know what's real in your forecast. You're curious about every deal and look into it yourself, so you and your team always know where you stand.

  • Take ownership. If a deal stalls, you reach out to the champion yourself. If it needs a workshop, you're happy to run it. You do what the deal needs.

  • Help your reps grow. You make coaching, training and deal reviews part of the team's week, and nothing motivates you more than seeing your AEs succeed.

  • Bring our way of selling to life. You know the product well and sell in an inquisitive, consultative and educative way, so your team learns it from you.


Who you are

  • You've carried a quota, closed complex B2B or enterprise deals, and still enjoy selling.

  • You're entrepreneurial and find creative ways to reach a goal.

  • You like to check things for yourself and ask good questions, including of your own team.

  • You love learning and are excited to adapt to how we sell rather than bringing a ready-made playbook.

  • Building a team excites you more than your own quota.


This might not be the right fit if…

  • you'd prefer to focus purely on people management and step away from deals.

  • you'd rather stick to one proven playbook than adapt it.

  • you'd rather keep your own quota than build a team.

  • you prefer to rely on your team's forecast without digging into it.


Why now

Our Go-To-Market team will grow significantly over the next year. You'd join early enough to shape how we lead sales, at a point where you can already see it working. Together with our sales leadership, you'll build your team and help define what great sales management looks like at Lio.

title: Electronics Engineering Manager
descriptionHtml:
About IonQ: 

IonQ, Inc. [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance.

Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before.  

The Role

We are looking for an Electronics Engineering Manager to lead the electronics function within our Systems team at IonQ. You will lead a team of three electronics engineers and grow it as our programmes scale. The team designs, builds and tests the electronics subsystems behind our mission to build the most performant quantum computers.

This is a player-coach role, with roughly 60% of your time spent leading the team and 40% on hands-on design work. You will set the technical direction for our electronics deliverables and build a team that can deliver them reliably, from experimental prototypes to rack-ready production systems.

Responsibilities 

You will own the electronics roadmap for current and next-generation quantum systems. That covers schematic capture and PCB layout through to board and system-level test, and the drive architecture for QPU designs.

You will balance hands-on technical leadership with people management, planning and coordination across teams. As the main electronics contact for the physics, firmware, mechanical and systems teams, you will turn complex physical requirements into clear, achievable engineering plans, and you will keep improving the tooling, workflow and capability of the team.Key responsibilities include: 

  • Team leadership: Lead and develop a team of three electronics engineers and play a key role in growing it through hiring. Set clear goals, run regular 1:1s and performance reviews, and build a culture of technical excellence and accountability.
  • Technical direction: Own the architecture of the electronics subsystems, including mixed-signal design, high-speed digital and signal integrity. Approve key design decisions and lead design reviews.
  • Delivery and planning: Plan, prioritise and track electronics workstreams against programme milestones, managing resourcing, schedules, risks and dependencies, and report progress to stakeholders.
  • Quality and process: Set and improve design standards, review processes, verification and test strategy (simulation, bench test, system integration) and documentation practices.
  • Productisation: Lead the move from experimental prototypes to robust, manufacturable, rack-ready production systems, working with suppliers and contract manufacturers as needed.

Requirements 

To succeed, you will need around ten years of experience in electronics design, with a strong background in high-speed and mixed-signal electronics, proven experience leading engineers and a track record of taking hardware from concept through prototype to production on schedule. You should be able to give credible technical guidance while growing the team around you, and bring a high level of attention to detail to your own work and to the designs you review.

You will be comfortable in a fast-moving, highly technical environment and know when to use waterfall or agile delivery in a hardware setting. Experience with Jira and Smartsheet, exposure to cryogenic environments, RF/microwave engineering (up to 500 MHz) or Python-based test automation, and familiarity with the Sinara/ARTIQ ecosystem in a quantum or physics research setting would all be an advantage.


You’d be a great fit with:

  • Engineering leadership experience: A track record of managing or technically leading electronics engineers, including hiring, mentoring and performance management.
  • Strong hardware design background: Hands-on experience with mixed-signal and high-speed digital design, SPICE modelling and lab verification (oscilloscopes, spectrum analysers).
  • Altium expertise: Experience with complex schematics, rigid-flex designs and advanced signal-integrity constraints, and the ability to review and guide others' designs.
  • FPGA and high-performance hardware: Familiarity with Xilinx/Intel toolchains (Vivado/Quartus) and carriers such as the BittWare XUP series or Sinara/ARTIQ hardware.
  • High-speed interfaces: Knowledge of SFP+/QSFP-DD interfaces, 10/100G Ethernet and high-speed differential pair routing.

Compensation will vary based on individual factors such as education, qualifications, and experience of the final candidate(s), specific office location, and calibration against relevant market data and internal team equity. Posted base salary figures are subject to change as new market data becomes available. Our benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans, matching 401(k), unlimited PTO and paid holidays, parental/adoption leave, legal insurance, and a home technology stipend. Details of participation in these benefit plans will be provided when a candidate receives an offer of employment. 

At IonQ, we believe in fair treatment, access, opportunity, and advancement for all while striving to identify and eliminate barriers. We empower employees to thrive by fostering a culture of autonomy, productivity, and respect. We are dedicated to creating an environment where individuals can feel welcomed, respected, supported, and valued.
 
We are committed to equity and justice. We welcome different voices and viewpoints and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, ancestry, physical and/or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, marital status, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, transgender status, age, sexual orientation, military or veteran status, or any other basis protected by law. title: Energy Markets - France (CDD)
descriptionHtml:
At Axle Energy, we’re building the infrastructure that will underpin the decarbonised energy system. Our software moves energy usage to times when electricity is cheap and green, by controlling vehicle charging, heating systems, and home batteries. We control hundreds of thousands of energy assets.

We’re building in a legacy industry and moving gigawatt-hours of electrons in the real world, but we operate at lightning speed, and we’re growing the team to meet customer demand.

We’re proud to be supported by world-leading investors, including Energize Capital and Accel.

Read more about what we’re building here.

France is one of the most important flexibility markets in Europe. This role is critical to accelerating Axle’s growth in France.

About the role

Axle has quickly become the leader in our operational markets, and we’re now looking to expand our reach in France.

At the core of our market expansion plans is market analysis. To maximise future revenue, we spend a lot of time understanding the value of flexibility in power markets around the world.

We are looking for a technical individual (data scientist, analyst or engineer) with strong knowledge of the French electricity markets and an instinct for commercial value.

You will become Axle’s internal expert on French power markets: understanding the market rules, modelling the value, and building relationships with system operators and regulators. We’re scrappy about method and rigorous about conclusions.

You will speak fluent French and English. Other European languages will also be an asset.

What you will be doing

  • Developing a deep understanding of French energy markets and grid dynamics to understand how trading, compensation, penalties and cash flow work

  • Jumping on the phone with grid operators, regulators and market stakeholders to validate hypotheses and make sense of data

  • Building and optimising models of wholesale/NEBCO, capacity, balancing, ancillary services and local flexibility markets in France to forecast what different assets can earn

  • Sizing the revenue opportunity across markets and products to shape where we expand next

  • Building and evaluating different strategies for cycling a battery or load-shifting an EV charger

  • Monitoring and shaping energy regulation to accelerate the growth of flexibility.

This is an opportunity to gain unique domain expertise and build the quantitative case for first-of-a-kind projects across the world.

What we think you need to be successful

  • Deep quantitative and modelling ability (Python, SQL)

  • Exceptional communication and the ability to turn data into actionable commercial insights

  • Comfort moving fast and making decisions in an evolving environment

  • Deep knowledge of French electricity markets (NEBCO, Mécanisme de Capacité, Mécanisme d’Ajustement, ancillary services…)

  • Relationships with regulators, grid operators and other stakeholders (CRE, DGEC, RTE, Enedis, etc.) are a plus

What’s in it for you

This is a 12 month fixed-term contract (CDD). Compensation is highly competitive and dependent on experience.

We operate with a deliberately flat structure and aim to keep pay equitable across the company, with a 1:1 median ratio between founder and team compensation.

Bi-annual retreats to strengthen team connection & shared purpose.

You’ll be based in France. To maximise collaboration, we ask that you spend ~1 week per month working from our London office.

The opportunity to directly shape the future of energy markets and accelerate the transition to a low-carbon world.

We are extremely keen to build a diverse team, and we’re particularly eager to hear from candidates who don't fit the traditional role stereotypes. If you’re motivated by our mission, please do reach out, even if you feel you might not ‘check all the boxes’.

Interview process

  1. Initial interview

  2. Take-home exercise

  3. Final interview (in-person)

  4. Offer, references, and welcome to the team!

title: Energy Procurement & Policy
descriptionHtml:
About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The team

Mistral Cloud builds and operates the infrastructure that powers Mistral's AI. The Data Centers team signs long-term leases for data center capacity developed by third-party operators, sources the GPUs that fill those halls, and runs the workloads that train and serve Mistral's models. Today the team is around 40 people, mainly based in Paris with some remote members, and operates roughly 200 MW of existing capacity across France. Key partners include Éclairion in France and EcoDC in Sweden, which is currently delivering Mistral's first Swedish data center.

The team sits at the center of an ambitious roadmap: Mistral has publicly committed to securing one gigawatt of data center capacity globally by 2030. With 200 MW already online, roughly 800 MW remain to be secured over the next five years. Every megawatt needs power, and power is this role's domain.

The Role

Mistral's data centers will consume hundreds of megawatts of electricity. This hire makes sure that power is reliable and affordable. You will define and execute Mistral's energy procurement strategy: structuring agreements with utilities, hedging against volatile spot prices, and tracking the regulatory changes that affect where and how data centers can be powered. The role also touches energy policy and community relations in the regions where Mistral operates.

This is a hybrid seat. Roughly half of the work is commercial: procurement contracts, hedging instruments, and price risk management. The other half is policy and positioning: monitoring regulation, engaging with grid operators and local authorities, and helping Mistral build the social license to operate large data centers across Europe.

What You Will Do

  • Define and execute Mistral's energy procurement strategy across European data center sites

  • Negotiate power purchase agreements and procurement contracts with utilities

  • Structure hedging agreements to limit exposure to volatile spot power prices

  • Monitor energy regulation and policy developments that affect data center siting, grid connection, and power pricing

  • Engage with grid operators, regulators, and local communities in regions where Mistral builds and operates data centers

What We're Looking For

  • You have procured energy at scale. You have structured power purchase agreements, utility contracts, or hedging instruments for industrial or infrastructure-scale consumers.

  • You understand European energy markets. You know how power pricing, grid connection, and regulation work across the markets where Mistral operates.

  • You can read a regulatory brief. You have tracked and interpreted energy or infrastructure policy and translated it into commercial implications.

  • You communicate across disciplines. You work effectively with engineers, finance, legal, and external stakeholders, and can explain complex energy concepts to non-specialists.

What We Offer

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page.

Privacy Policy

Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy.

With our hot coral cards and get-paid-early feature, combined with financial education on social media and our award winning customer service, we have a long history of creating magical moments for our customers!

We’re not about selling products - we want to solve problems and change lives through Monzo ❤️

📍London or Remote (UK) or Barcelona, Spain (Hybrid) 

Engineering at Monzo

Monzo has successfully launched in Ireland and is expanding across Europe. We're now entering the next phase of our journey: building and scaling a multi-market European bank.

The EU Engineering organisation sits at the centre of that ambition. We are responsible for helping Monzo launch, grow and operate across Europe, navigating everything from product-market fit and customer growth to regulatory requirements, localisation and operational scale.

Unlike most engineering organisations at Monzo, EU does not own a single product area. We work horizontally across the company, partnering with teams across Payments, Core Banking, Growth, Wealth, Customer Operations, Fincrime, Platform and many others to bring Monzo's products to new markets and deliver great customer experiences locally.

As an Engineering Director, you'll lead a distributed engineering organisation across the UK, Spain and remote locations. You'll partner closely with Product, Design, Data, Operations, Risk, Compliance and executive stakeholders to solve complex problems that span organisational boundaries.

Success in this role comes through influence, relationships and organisational leadership as much as execution. You'll need to build alignment across a wide range of teams, create clarity in ambiguity, and help Monzo discover what works in new markets while establishing the foundations that allow us to scale across Europe.

This is one of Monzo's most strategically important areas and a unique opportunity to help build a European bank from the ground up.

What you’ll work on

  • Lead a distributed engineering organisation spanning multiple squads, markets and countries.
  • Build and develop Engineering Managers, Senior Engineering Managers and senior technical leaders.
  • Partner with Product, Design, Data, Research, Operations, Risk and Compliance leaders to define and execute Monzo's European strategy.
  • Drive alignment and execution across numerous collectives to ensure Europe receives the capabilities it needs to succeed.
  • Shape how Monzo approaches market expansion, localisation, regulatory requirements and multi-market product development.
  • Influence priorities and outcomes across teams that do not directly report to you.
  • Create clarity and momentum in highly ambiguous problem spaces where ownership and solutions are not always obvious.
  • Design and evolve organisational structures, operating models and planning processes that allow Monzo to scale effectively across Europe.
  • Help identify and validate product-market fit in new markets while balancing short-term delivery and long-term strategic investments.
  • Partner closely with executive leadership to shape the future of Monzo's European business.

You should apply if

  • You have experience leading large engineering organisations through other leaders, including Engineering Managers, Senior Engineering Managers and senior individual contributors.
  • You have successfully operated in highly complex organisations where outcomes depend on collaboration across many teams and functions.
  • You are exceptional at building relationships and influencing without direct authority.
  • You can navigate ambiguity and create clarity where goals, ownership or priorities are not yet fully defined.
  • You have experience scaling organisations through periods of rapid growth, organisational change or market expansion.
  • You enjoy solving organisational and business problems, not just technical ones.You can balance strategy and execution, translating ambitious goals into tangible outcomes.
  • You are comfortable making decisions in environments where there is rarely a perfect answer.
  • You have a strong track record of building high-performing leadership teams and developing future leaders.
  • You are energised by the challenge of building something new and helping shape the future of Monzo's international expansion.

The interview process

After an informal ~30 min recruiter call our interview process involves 2 main stages: 

  1. Initial Call (1 hour) You'll meet with one of our senior engineering leaders. They'll ask you about your previous experience, in particular people leadership, product delivery and technical leadership. They’ll ask example based questions (‘Tell me about a time when…’)
  2. Loop Stage - This is one stage with 4 interviews (totalling 4 hours) split between a collaboration with one of our engineers on a technical exercise, as well as execution and leadership interviews.

At all stages we’ll create space for you to ask as many questions as you have, you’re interviewing us as well!

Our average process takes around 3-4 weeks but we will always work around your availability. You will have the chance to speak to our recruitment team at various points during your process but if you do have any specific questions ahead of this please contact us on

How we work 💻:

Locations & Flexible Working (If you're in the UK) : 

Our main tech hub is in London, but our engineers live everywhere in the UK— from Brighton to the Western Isles. 

We value meeting in person but there’s no pressure to come into the office, even if you're nearby. We believe you'll do your best work if you are where you want to be. If you live outside of London and we ask you to come into the office, Monzo will support you with the costs. ✨

Our offices are naturally social, especially Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays, which happen to line up with our twice-weekly Monzo lunches & treat Thursdays 🍽️. Teams also schedule time together often for work and play – in or around the office, or online.

Set up a work schedule that delivers impact and fits your life.

At Monzo, we value connections, flexibility, and wellbeing. We keep our meetings during core hours to stay connected and believe in maintaining work/life balance. 

You’ll be empowered to manage your work in a way that suits you and your team, giving you the freedom for children drop-offs and pick-ups, walking your dog or adventurous cat, avoiding peak commuting times or gym slots, appointments, or supporting your family in an emergency. 🕒✨

Work the way that works for you with Monzo! 💼

What’s in it for you

✈️ We can help you relocate to the UK or Spain

✅ We can sponsor visas for the UK (not Spain)

📍This role can be based in our London office, but we're open to distributed working within the UK (with ad hoc meetings in London).

⏰ We offer flexible working hours and trust you to work enough hours to do your job well, at times that suit you and your team.

📚Learning budget of £1,000 ( a year for books, training courses and conferences

Equal opportunities for everyone

Diversity and inclusion are a priority for us and we’re making sure we have lots of support for all of our people to grow at Monzo. At Monzo, we’re embracing diversity by fostering an inclusive environment for all people to do the best work of their lives with us. This is integral to our mission of making money work for everyone. You can read more in our blog, 2026 Diversity and Inclusion Report and 2025 Gender Pay Gap Report.

We’re an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to age, ethnicity, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, or veteran, neurodiversity or disability status.

title: Engineering Manager, Alwin Agent Runtime
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a skilled and passionate Engineering Manager to join our Alwin Agents Runtime Team in the Amsterdam office. Working in a bootstrapped and profitable scaleup, you'll have the unique opportunity to lead a team building the intelligence layer that automates the assurance lifecycle and brings AI directly into the workflows of auditors worldwide.


Why DataSnipper?

The hardest AI problems aren't about getting an answer fast. They're about getting one people can trust.

We believe trust is essential to how society works. Every day, we rely on information that's been independently verified, from financial statements to the products we buy, to the sustainability claims companies make. Behind that trust are audit and finance professionals who examine evidence, verify information and hold organizations accountable.

At DataSnipper, we build AI solutions that empower those professionals. By making evidence easier to trace and verify, we help them focus on the judgment and expertise that make their work so important.

For our product and engineering team, this is where things get exciting. In audit, a plausible answer isn't good enough. Every output has to be explainable and traceable back to its source. We've just launched a brand new agentic platform, Alwin by DataSnipper. AI agents running in the cloud across hundreds of documents at once, reasoning across PDF, Word and Excel, with a full audit trail behind every step. There are lots of greenfield problems ahead, and real room to shape what we build and how we build it.

And we build at scale. More than 600,000 professionals across 3,000+ organizations in 175 countries rely on DataSnipper, including Fortune 500 companies, government agencies and all Big Four audit firms. In 2025 alone, the DataSnipper platform delivered more than $1.4 billion in productivity savings to is customers. Backed by a $100 million Series B led by Index Ventures, at a $1 billion valuation, and as proud members of 1% for the Planet, we care about how we grow, not just how fast.

If you want to build AI that professionals trust with work that really matters, this is your chance to help shape the future of audit and finance and do the best work of your career along the way.


What You Will Do:

  • Lead an engineering team through outcomes, not tasks; set clear goals with the team and trust them to figure out how.

  • Make the team measurably better; raise the engineering bar, grow engineers into bigger problems, and address performance issues directly when they arise.

  • Drive a step change in what the team can do with AI; not just shipping faster, but tackling harder problems, raising quality, and expanding what the team can credibly own.

  • Lead the team responsible for building AI-powered agents that automate assurance workflows, from risk assessment and evidence gathering to control testing and documentation generation.

  • Own the technical direction and architecture of the Alwin Agent Runtime, ensuring agents are reliable, observable, secure, and effective in real customer workflows.

  • Guide the team in designing and scaling agentic systems that combine LLMs, document intelligence, business workflows, and human oversight.

  • Lead the adoption of AI-assisted engineering practices and contribute to how DataSnipper leverages AI across the broader engineering organization.

  • Help shape the team's scope as it evolves, including expanding ownership areas and standing up new teams when needed.

  • Foster a culture of experimentation, learning, documentation, and operational excellence.

What You Bring:

Preferred Qualifications

title: Engineering Manager
descriptionHtml:
We have real traction and proven scale, and we're now setting up how engineering works for our next wave of European growth. You would lead one of the teams doing it, and shape the practices the others follow.

ABOUT THE ROLE

You would lead one of our product engineering teams: what it ships, how it runs, and how the people in it grow. Product and engineering together are ~25 people, so there is nowhere to hide and nothing you can't reach.

It's a hands-on role. One week you're in a design review, the next - in a few Claude-enabled contributions, the next - in performance conversations, and most weeks - all of that combined. You should love zooming in and out, from feedback on an API spec to a quarter's priorities. Your team trusts your technical judgement because you still use it.

Beyond your team, you would shape how engineering works at Insify together with the other Engineering Managers, a Staff Engineer and the VP Engineering: architecture, product discovery, how engineers grow.


What you'll be doing
  • Leading a team of product engineers end to end: what you ship, how it performs in production, and who you hire and grow to get there
  • Bringing architecture and product thinking into the team's daily work, so that new product demands turn into platform capabilities that scale across countries and insurance products, rather than one-off builds
  • Running product discovery with your team: working with the Insurance, Operations and Growth teams on what to build, and saying no when the answer is no
  • Shaping company-wide engineering practices alongside the other Engineering Managers: ways of working, architecture & technology practices, the growth framework
  • Challenging our ideas and bringing your own. We encourage each other to act this way, so you can expect the same from others

    • What you'll need
  • You've managed a team of engineers before, including hiring, feedback and growing people. It doesn't have to be for long, but it has to be real and you have to want more of it
  • Years of hands-on experience designing and running distributed systems, including time spent maintaining what you designed. You can still carry an architecture discussion and review a design, and your team would trust your judgement on it
  • A track record of shaping what gets built, not only how: you've run or driven product discovery, cut scope, and can show the decisions that followed
  • Ownership & impact instinct - when needed you go beyond your team's boundaries to get to results
  • You set the bar for AI adoption on your team. You use it to real effect in your own work, you're honest about where it helped and where it fell short, and you're the first to try new tools, bringing the ones that stick to your engineers.

    • Nice to have
  • You are eager to scale your experience beyond your team - to create wider organisational impact
  • Experience building B2B products, especially in insurance & fintech
  • Experience working on a product distributed across different country markets
  • Experience with TypeScript and AWS

    • Our stack
  • TypeScript across the board, running on AWS with infrastructure as code, in a single monorepo.

    • None of this is a hard requirement, and you don't need to know all of our stack. We care more about how you reason about systems and teams than which tools you have used. Strong on most of it? Apply.


    We offer
  • Competitive compensation. We offer a salary in the range of 85k-110k EUR plus performance-based equity grants
  • Hybrid. 3 days in the office, 2 from home, up to 4 weeks a year from abroad, 25 holiday days
  • Pension. 6% employer contribution
  • Wellbeing budget. €50 net a month via Epassi, from the gym to takeaway, rolls over
  • Learning and coaching. Internal leadership programs and coaching
  • Central Amsterdam office. Shared lunches, dogs, Friday drinks, high-spec MacBook Pro

    • HOW WE HIRE

    Five conversations, each with a clear purpose, and you hear where you stand after every one:

    • Leadership. We look at your experience with performance management, personal development and building teams.
    • Code Review. You review a feature with two of our engineers.
    • System Design. An architecture problem close to what we deal with.
    • Values Interview. We look at your approach to work, and how it adds to our Values.
    • Meet the Founder.

    You get the outcome within three days of your last round, with specific feedback either way.

    ABOUT INSIFY

    Insify is a high-growth scale-up backed by €43M in total funding from world-class investors like Accel, Munich Re Ventures, and Formula 1 champion Nico Rosberg. In five years, we've expanded from the Netherlands into France and Germany, and we're just getting started. Our mission: become the European leader in AI-powered SME insurance.

    We aren't just building a company; we're leading a revolution. Our culture is intense, high-stakes, and mission-driven. We hire smart, ambitious "owners" who possess a relentless drive to win. This is an environment for those who thrive on challenges, value intellectual honesty, and share our mindset of becoming a global category leader.

    Our founding team consists of seasoned entrepreneurs who have previously built iconic businesses like HelloFresh, Bloomon, and SumUp. We bring that same bias for speed, scale, and high standards to one of the most structurally broken experiences in financial services. Together, we combine that deep fintech and e-commerce expertise with cutting-edge AI to stay ahead of the curve.

title: Engineering Manager - CDI Paris - Theodo HealthTech
descriptionHtml:
L’histoire du groupe Theodo et son succès
Theodo accompagne depuis 2009 les entreprises innovantes dans la conception, le développement et le déploiement de produits digitaux ingénieux - tels que la plateforme TF1+, l'application LCL Pro ou l'application France Identité Numérique - en tirant parti du meilleur de la technologie et de l’approche Lean.

Theodo connait une croissance exceptionnelle depuis 15 ans : nos équipes rassemblent plus de 750 Theodoers, principalement des Software Engineers, passionnés de technologie et d’amélioration continue. En 2025, le groupe Theodo génère 100M€ de CA. Chez Theodo HealthTech, l'entité experte en santé, nous accompagnons tous les acteurs de la santé dans le développement des dispositifs médicaux digitaux sur-mesure. Grâce à notre expérience du Lean et de la tech, combinées à notre connaissance de la santé, nous concevons et développons des dispositifs médicaux numériques qui s'intègrent dans le parcours de soins des patients (thérapies digitales - DTx, essais cliniques virtualisés, parcours de soins digitalisés). Notre but est de réaliser des produits qui changent la vie de leurs utilisateurs, qu'ils soient soignants ou patients.
Ton équipe : Chez Theodo, les techs travaillent en équipes projet, constituées en fonction des besoins de chaque client, réunissant Software Engineers, Tech Lead et Product Manager. Ensemble, ils collaborent étroitement avec le client, avec des échanges réguliers pour partager vos avancées, approfondir la compréhension de son problème et faire évoluer le produit au plus près des besoins de ses utilisateurs. En tant qu’Engineering Manager, ton rôle est de manager jusqu’à 4 tech leads, soit de chapeauter la réussite de 4 projets, en binôme avec un(e) Group Project Manager. Tes futures missions : Le besoin actuel porte sur des missions “grands-comptes” avec des produits et architectures complexes, développées par plusieurs squads de Theodo : - Manager & faire progresser les Tech Leads : tu accompagnes 1 à 4 Tech Leads dans leur montée en compétence et leur épanouissement. - Assurer le delivery technique : tu garantis la qualité du code (3S : stabilité, sécurité, vitesse), la tenue des jalons et la robustesse de l’architecture. - Contribuer au développement business : tu participes aux discussions stratégiques avec nos clients (DSI, sponsors…), tu aides à identifier des opportunités et tu es acteur de l’avant-vente avec nos sales. Les problématiques et les technos sont très différentes d’un projet à l’autre, voici quelques exemples : - Hub Santé : lancé par l’Agence du Numérique en Santé en 2024, vise à connecter en temps réel les 83 SAMU, SMUR, SDIS et autres acteurs de l’urgence, dans un écosystème historiquement fragmenté. Accompagnée par une équipe de 3 experts Theodo, l’ANS a déployé une plateforme nationale d’interopérabilité permettant une coordination critique plus fluide et sécurisée. Résultats : +10 SAMU connectés dès la phase pilote, interopérabilité effective sur plusieurs périmètres et conformité HDS maintenue. - Vidal : référence centenaire de l’information médicale, a développé avec Theodo un assistant médical basé sur l’IA générative pour fournir aux professionnels de santé des réponses fiables en un temps record et sécuriser la prescription. En 8 semaines, une équipe de 4 experts Theodo a conçu un POC de chatbot RAG connecté à la base Vidal, capable de réduire le temps de recherche tout en garantissant traçabilité et fiabilité des sources. Objectif : renforcer la confiance des praticiens et faire entrer Vidal dans l’ère du service médical “fonctionnel”. Tes perspectives d’évolutions : Perspectives d’évolution moyen terme (1 - 2 ans) : - Manageriale : VP Tech ou Group Manager - Technique : Architecte senior - Business/Influence : Thought Leader (animer une communauté tech) ou Intrapreneur (porter une nouvelle offre) Une méthodologie basée sur l’apprentissage continu : Chez Theodo, nous avons construit notre approche tech autour d’une conviction forte : on développe d’abord les personnes, avant de développer les produits. Notre Lean Tech® System met l’accent sur l’apprentissage continu : tu évolueras dans un environnement qui investit sur le long terme, où l’objectif est de te permettre de progresser chaque jour, tout en construisant des produits utiles et performants pour nos clients. Profil recherché : - 7 à 14 ans d’expérience professionnelle, avec une expérience confirmée en management d’équipes tech et en environnement ESN / conseil. - Basé(e) en région parisienne, avec une préférence pour une présence majoritaire au bureau, attendue pour un rôle stratégique et managérial. Hard skills - Solide expertise technologique (Java / Spring Boot et/ou Angular) permettant d’être crédible et légitime auprès des équipes, sans être attendu·e sur le code au quotidien. - Capacité à concevoir des architectures évolutives et à arbitrer des choix techniques dans des contextes grands comptes complexes. - Expérience significative en management d’équipes techniques, avec la capacité à débloquer des Tech - Leads sur des problématiques techniques complexes. - Capacité d’analyse et de résolution de problèmes complexes, avec un impact transverse dans l’organisation. - Intérêt pour l’IA générative et son usage dans la conception et le développement de produits digitaux. Soft skills - Leadership affirmé et posture pédagogique pour embarquer, inspirer et faire progresser des équipes exigeantes. - Orientation marquée business et création de valeur : chez Theodo, nous ne faisons pas de la tech pour la tech. - Aisance relationnelle et communicationnelle, avec la capacité d’adresser tous niveaux d’interlocuteurs, y compris C-level, et de mener des conversations exigeantes. Le process de recrutement : - Call de qualification (30 min) avec un membre de l’équipe recrutement - Cultural fit (1h) avec le même recruteur - Test technique de refactoring (à la maison + débrief 1h) - Entretien modélisation (1h) - Simulation vente d’architecture à un DSI (1h) - Final avec un dirigeant - Prise de référencePourquoi rejoindre Theodo HealthTech ? L’environnement: 💼 Rejoindre un groupe de 750 personnes avec de nombreuses possibilités d’évolutions cross-entités 🤝 Chaque Theodoer est accompagné par un coach interne. Son objectif : t’épauler dans ton quotidien et parler objectifs de carrière via des séances de coaching hebdomadaires. 🎯 Participation à des projets associatifs grâce à la Fondation Theodo (Ada Tech School, Code Phoenix, Article 1…) 🎉 Soirées mensuelles, keynotes et week-end d’entreprise annuel Le package : 📈 Actionnariat salarié pour être associé à la réussite du groupe 💸 Prime d’intéressement indexée sur la croissance de Theodo 🖥 Budget équipement (ordinateur, smartphone, écouteurs…) 🧒 Des avantages fournis par notre CSE (sport avec Gymlib,...) 🏖 5 semaines + 8 à 12 RTT/an 🩺 Mutuelle (SideCare) prise en charge à 50% 🍽 Carte ticket-restaurants Swile 🧒 Aides et places en crèche réservées Prêt à nous rejoindre ?

title: Engineering Manager - Compilers
descriptionHtml:
About Fractile

Fractile was founded in 2022 on the bet that, eventually, the world’s most capable AI systems would be limited in their impact by the time taken to produce useful outputs. We bet everything on the logical conclusion: that the only way to truly unlock this latent value, to make speed viable at scale, was to radically re-invent the hardware that we run our frontier AI models on. Ever since, we have been building chips and systems that tackle this problem: how to efficiently generate output at thousands of tokens per second, while handling the complexity and capacity challenges of operating large models at very long contexts.

 

The workloads that push to the limits of the current frontier are already transformational; it is the technical and economic limits on inference speed that are constraining progress. The defining work of the 21st century will be marked by the engine of inference delivering immense and diffuse chains of intellectual inquiry, in drug discovery, in software engineering, in materials discovery, in any field where progress is driven by deep reasoning and intelligence to resolve complex problems.

The role

Fractile is building a full-stack AI accelerator from the ground up, and the compiler team sits at the heart of how we deliver performance. As the Engineering Manager for Compilers, you will build and lead a team of 10+ engineers developing the compiler stack for our novel AI acceleration hardware, with direct responsibility for enabling industry-leading LLM inference performance on Fractile's accelerators. This is a hands-on technical leadership role in a fast-moving, collaborative environment where the compiler team works closely with hardware, driver, runtime and ML engineers across the stack. If you want to shape the architecture of a compiler from first principles, build a world-class team around it, and have your work directly determine the performance of next-generation AI hardware, this is the role.

What we’re looking for:

  • Proven track record of leadership experience managing a high-performance development team and delivering consistently outstanding outcomes.

  • Proven experience in compiler development, with experience of machine learning compilers and industry standard technologies such as MLIR or TVM being a significant advantage.

  • Up-to-date knowledge of machine learning techniques and technologies

  • A good understanding of computer architecture and performance optimisation techniques.

  • Excellent C/C++ skills and solid experience of industry standard development tools and technologies.

  • A creative and innovative mindset, and a willingness to take ownership and drive results in a fast-paced environment.

What you’re signing up for:

This is a young company doing hard things, at the intersection of novel silicon and the software stack that makes it useful. You'll be building and leading a compiler team as the hardware it targets is still taking shape, which means making architectural decisions against a specification first, then a simulator, then early silicon. The IR design, the lowering strategy, the execution model: you'll help define all of it before you can run it on real hardware. That takes comfort with ambiguity and the ability to make good calls with incomplete information. If that sounds frustrating, this probably isn't the role. If that sounds like the interesting part, we should talk.

The boundaries here are soft by design. The compiler team works closely with hardware architects, kernel engineers, runtime teams and ML researchers. You'll need to understand enough of what sits above and below your layer to make good decisions at the boundary, and to build a team that can do the same. That breadth is a feature of the job, not a distraction from it.

You'll be there when the first model runs end to end on Fractile silicon. When the lowering strategy you helped design produces a result the hardware team didn't think was possible yet. When the team you hired and grew ships something that goes into every rack we sell.

We want a team that reflects the world it's building for, and we welcome applicants from every background, including those whose path here hasn't been straight. We care that you're energised by this kind of work, that you build and develop great engineers, and that you make the people around you better.

Come build it with us.

What We Offer

  • Competitive salary: A competitive salary reflective of your experience and the specialist nature of the role.

  • Equity & Ownership: meaningful equity so everyone shares in the value creation

  • Benefits: Private Medical, Dental and Vision, Contributory Pension, 25 Days holiday plus bank holidays and Life/Critical Illness Insurance.

  • Diverse & fun office: we believe the hardest problems get solved by the broadest range of minds. We are committed to Equal Employment Opportunity through attracting and retaining a diverse team and building an inclusive environment.

Fractile is seeking to increase the clock speed of global progress, one chip at a time. We’ve recently raised $220M from investors including Founders Fund and Accel and our most important work lies ahead. Join us!

 

Export controls

Our work involves technologies subject to UK, US and other international export control regulations. Certain roles may require additional eligibility checks to ensure compliance with applicable law. We'll be transparent about this throughout the hiring process.

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The team

Mistral is building a sovereign AI cloud for Europe. Our customers in finance, healthcare, and the public sector run frontier models on European-jurisdiction infrastructure, and the Cloud Platform team builds the systems that make that possible — compute orchestration, Kubernetes, bare metal, storage, networking, and the datacenter fleet that runs it all.

European Compute Units let enterprises commit to multi-year capacity on that infrastructure, and we are scaling toward a gigawatt of compute across Europe by 2030. You will design and ship the layer every sovereign AI deployment depends on and shape the team building it.

The Role

A datacenter is not a cloud until software makes it one. You will lead the team that turns arriving hardware into accepted clusters.

Cabling validation, burn-in, firmware, deployment validation, software stack install — all of it automated, none of it click-ops. Your KPI is time to acceptance: the hours between a rack being physically installed and it serving customer workloads. Across the industry that number is measured in weeks. You will drive it toward days, then hours, as we scale toward a gigawatt of compute across Europe.

This is a founding leadership role at the intersection of hardware and software. Early on it is deliberately hands-on: most of your time in the code and the architecture, some of it on datacenter floors, because the automation has to survive contact with the machines it runs on.

But the job is building and leading a team from day one — hiring your first engineers, coaching them, setting their growth paths, and running the rituals that keep quality high. As the team grows, the balance shifts toward people leadership, and you decide how fast. You shape this new team's charter and set the standard for how every future Mistral datacenter comes online.

What You Will Do

  • Build the delivery pipeline in Go: provisioning, configuration, validation, burn-in, network bring-up, software stack install.

  • Build the team from scratch: make the first hires, onboard and coach them, own their performance and growth paths — and set the tooling standards and the playbook every future site reuses.

  • Own time-to-acceptance and drive it down relentlessly — measure it, break it down, kill the slowest step first.

  • Work shoulder-to-shoulder with Hardware Design and Fleet Health — reliability starts at delivery.

  • Handle GPU fleets at scale: H100 and GB200-class nodes, InfiniBand and RoCE fabrics, and the failure modes they bring.

  • Partner with Product Managers and the datacenter org to plan delivery waves against capacity commitments.

What We're Looking For

  • You have automated bare-metal fleets — you have written the software that turns racks into clusters. If you have done it by hand, you resented it and scripted it.

  • Hardware fluency: servers, GPUs, NICs, switches, firmware — you can read a parts list and a topology diagram.

  • 8+ years building backend or infrastructure systems, with at least 2 years leading engineers — real people leadership: you have hired, coached, and grown engineers, not just set technical direction.

  • Deep Linux: you are comfortable well below the application layer.

  • You have shipped production systems in Go. Not dabbled. Shipped.

  • Willing to travel to datacenter sites when the work demands it.

  • A low-ego, team-first mindset. We care less about your exact domain and more about whether you are the kind of technical force other engineers want to work alongside.

What We Offer

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance.
