title: Strategy & Solutions Lead
descriptionHtml:
About us:

Causaly is redefining how humans acquire knowledge and develop insights in biomedicine. Our AI-powered platform enables researchers and decision-makers to discover and interpret evidence from millions of scientific publications, clinical trials, regulatory documents, and other complex data sources in minutes.

We are building the world’s most advanced biomedical knowledge platform, powered by a high-precision Knowledge Graph and GenAI capabilities. Our technology is already used by leading biopharmaceutical organizations to accelerate drug discovery, improve safety, and drive better decision-making.

Backed by top-tier investors including ICONIQ, Index Ventures, Pentech, and Marathon, we are scaling rapidly and expanding our product suite and market presence. 

About the Role

Causaly is hiring a Strategy and Solutions Lead to incubate and validate new growth opportunities at the intersection of AI, data, product, and our pharma and biotech customers across R&D and commercial functions.

This role focuses exclusively on new territory — new capabilities, solution lines, integrations, or market segments — where customer demand goes beyond what our product supports out of the box. The mandate is to turn ambiguous enterprise demand into scalable, repeatable solution plays grounded in real pharma workflows, drive executive decision-making, and then hand those plays into BAU teams once validated.

You will work directly with Causaly’s executive leadership and lead discussions with senior stakeholders across pharma R&D and commercial functions, as well as their data and technology teams, to shape strategic partnerships, solution architecture, and product decisions. You will operate with significant autonomy, owning opportunities from the first strategic conversation through to executive decision and handoff.

What You’ll Do

Own strategic “new territory” decisions

◆ Own intake and shaping of strategic enterprise opportunities that require new capabilities, integrations, packaging, or market positioning.

◆ Drive executive decisioning on whether to pursue, park, or decline opportunities, with clear rationale, options, and business and technical implications.

◆ Maintain a clear boundary between incubation work and BAU; ensure this team is only engaged where something new must be created.

Lead senior R&D and commercial conversations and translate demand into scalable solution paths

◆ Lead high-stakes discussions with senior stakeholders across pharma R&D (e.g. Discovery, Translational Science, Clinical Development) and commercial functions (e.g. Portfolio Strategy, New Product Planning, Medical Affairs, Market Access).

◆ Ground discovery in customers’ end-to-end workflows and decision points (e.g. target identification and validation, Target Product Profile development, candidate selection, indication expansion, lifecycle management) to define target state, success criteria, and constraints.

◆ Translate ambiguous asks into a solution concept and delivery path, including where Causaly creates value in the workflow, scope boundaries, sequencing, timelines, risks, dependencies, and mutual commitments.

◆ Shape expectations and commercial framing to ensure scalable commitments (what is standard, what is configurable, what requires investment, and what is out of scope).

Design and steer technical solutions

◆ Work with customer architecture, data, IT, and AI teams in working-level depth on Causaly’s platform capabilities, APIs, data model, and integration patterns (e.g. with internal data lakes, knowledge management systems, and enterprise AI tooling), going beyond high-level positioning to a solution design both sides can build against.

◆ Drive the solution design for new plays, including integration approach, data flows, security, and deployment model, and work alongside Causaly’s Engineering and Data teams through build, testing, and deployment, without being the engineer writing production code.

◆ Pressure-test technical feasibility early: review architectures, spot integration and data risks, and make informed calls on what can be configured, what needs to be built, and what effort it will take.

◆ Shape and evaluate technology partnerships (e.g. data providers, cloud and AI platforms, systems integrators), including strategic rationale, technical fit, integration approach, and joint solution design.

◆ Represent Causaly’s platform and roadmap credibly in executive and technical forums, clearly positioning what the platform does today, what is configurable, and where it is heading.

Build repeatable solution playbooks (incl. Private Data & integrations)

◆ Turn recurring demand into solution playbooks anchored in specific R&D and commercial workflows, including:

◇ Offering definition, use cases, and packaging

◇ Qualification and fit criteria

◇ Scoping templates and success plans

◇ Delivery blueprints, reference architectures, and enablement assets

◆ Standardise complex offerings (e.g. Private Data, enterprise integrations, and AI workflows on customer data) into productised motions with clear patterns, governance, and pilot-to-rollout pathways.

◆ Partner with Product, Engineering, and Data to define feasibility options and reference architectures, and surface clear product and investment recommendations.

Validate plays through lighthouse execution

◆ Co-sponsor a small number of lighthouse opportunities with Sales to validate new solution plays.

◆ Orchestrate early cross-functional work (pilot design, governance, decisioning) with the explicit goal of making the play transferable and repeatable, not owning delivery long-term.

Institutionalise and hand off into BAU

◆ Drive clean handoff of validated plays into BAU (Sales, CS, Delivery, Product), including training, assets, decision trees, and ownership clarity.

◆ Maintain a structured feedback loop into Product on product candidates, investment needs, and learned constraints from enterprise demand.

What We’re Looking For

◆ 7+ years’ experience at the intersection of pharma or life sciences strategy, AI and data, and enterprise customers, with a track record of leading discussions with senior R&D and commercial stakeholders and shaping ambiguous asks into scalable solutions.

◆ Strong fit from one of the following backgrounds:

◇ Life science strategy or AI consulting at Engagement Manager / Associate Partner level, with substantial R&D or commercial work and ownership of AI or data programmes from strategy through to scale-up

◇ Enterprise Solutions / Solutions Strategy roles in B2B SaaS serving pharma and biotech, particularly in AI-, data-, or platform-heavy products

◆ Deep understanding of end-to-end pharma R&D and commercial workflows and the decisions within them (e.g. target identification, Target Product Profile, candidate selection, indication expansion, launch and lifecycle planning), and of how data and AI can change them.

◆ Hands-on experience building, deploying, and/or integrating technology solutions in enterprise settings (e.g. data platforms, AI and LLM applications, API and system integrations). You have been close enough to the build to understand how a solution works, not just what it does, and have seen solutions through to production.

◆ Ability to read and challenge solution architectures, reason through data pipelines, APIs, and integration patterns, and understand how AI and LLM systems are built and evaluated (e.g. retrieval-augmented generation, agentic workflows, knowledge graphs).

◆ Experience turning complex, bespoke-seeming enterprise demand into repeatable playbooks (qualification criteria, scoping frameworks, pilot design, and BAU handoff).

◆ Strong judgement in making and defending pursue / park / decline recommendations based on product direction, feasibility, scalability, and business impact.

◆ Comfort driving executive decisioning (internally and on the customer side) across Product, Engineering, and GTM, and translating technical trade-offs into clear business choices.

Nice to Have

◆ Scientific or quantitative background (e.g. advanced degree in life sciences, engineering, or a related field).

◆ Experience on AI or GenAI programmes in pharma, from use-case definition through to scaled deployment.

◆ Prior experience in a technical capacity (e.g. forward deployed engineer, data scientist, software engineer, technical product manager).

◆ Familiarity with enterprise data governance in regulated environments (e.g. GxP, data privacy, information security reviews).

◆ Exposure to market expansion, new segment GTM, technology partnerships, or solution incubation.

  • Technical Investigation – Diagnose and troubleshoot technical issues, gather the right evidence and work confidently with Product and Engineering when deeper investigation is required.

  • Product Knowledge – Develop a strong understanding of Aveni’s products to support users effectively and confidently.

  • Launch & Cross-functional Collaboration – Work with Product, Marketing, Training & Enablement and Engineering to ensure Help Centre and Intercom content is accurate, and that customer documentation and Support readiness are in place for new features and product launches.

  • AI Support Optimisation – Take day-to-day ownership of optimising our AI customer support experience. At Aveni we use Intercom Fin, but experience with Zendesk AI or similar platforms is equally relevant. Author, test and continuously improve the content and instructions that power Fin; tune workflows, routing and hand-off paths; review customer conversations to identify new deflection and automation opportunities; and implement improvements that allow more requests to be resolved before reaching the Support team. Own regular reporting on AI involvement, resolution and deflection rates, using the data to identify trends, prioritise experiments and demonstrate the impact of changes.

  • Knowledge Management – Maintain and improve Help Centre content, FAQs and internal Support guidance, ensuring AI and human agents have accurate, useful knowledge to work from. Identify documentation gaps through conversation reviews, support trends and AI performance, and work with Product, Marketing and Training & Enablement to close them.

We’re looking for evidence that you have actively improved how an AI agent performs — for example by authoring and testing content, tuning workflows or routing, reviewing conversations for deflection opportunities, and using involvement, resolution or deflection reporting to drive measurable improvements. Direct Fin experience isn't essential; the track record matters more than the platform.

  • Experience maintaining customer-facing knowledge bases or Help Centres and turning support trends into clear, useful documentation.

Nice to Have

  • Previous experience in a B2B SaaS or fintech environment, particularly supporting complex or regulated customers.

  • Experience designing or running experiments to improve AI agents, automation or self-service journeys in a customer support environment.

  • Experience using support and AI metrics such as SLA, CSAT, involvement, resolution and escalation trends to identify and prioritise improvements.

  • Experience with incident and problem management practices, including escalation, stakeholder communication, root cause analysis and continuous improvement.

title: System Integration Senior Engineer (Platform Focus)
descriptionHtml:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building spacecraft for humanity.

The System Integration Senior Engineer will help lead the Nyx system end‑to‑end integration and verification, with a focus on functional platforms (Software in the Loop Platform, Processor in the Loop Platform, Hardware in the Loop Platform, Functional Simulation Facility). You will define and execute test plans, manage requirement traceability, analyse test results, and close verification evidence across SIL/PIL/HIL and physical test campaigns. Working closely with subsystem leads, AIT teams, and external partners, you will identify integration risks, resolve anomalies, and ensure that all mechanical functions perform safely and reliably throughout the mission profile. This position requires a rigorous systems mindset, strong understanding of mechanical behaviour in the space environment, and the ability to lead multidisciplinary verification activities to successful closure.

Key Responsibilities

In your capacity a System Integration Senior Engineer, your role will continuously evolve, but initially your day-to-day duties will include:

  • Ensure the definition and implementation of the Nyx Earth system integration and verification activities, which meets technical and programmatic requirements and considers the adequacy of model philosophy, facilities availability, planning and costing.

  • Define plans and specifications with clear Success Criteria and support the generation of test procedures with the Functional Platform team.

  • Drive the technical discussions, preparation, organization and execution of the system verification campaigns, to ensure the closure of all system verification aspects, including nominal and off nominal spacecraft behaviors.

  • Organise the different reviews for incremental progress and ultimate closure of verification events.

  • Generate reports and drive the closure of the Items for Verification and Validation covered by the campaign.

  • Collaborate with all Functional Chain responsible and engineering disciplines to prepare and perform the system activities.

  • Process the anomalies occurring during the verification campaign in coordination with the Product Assurance Team and the rest of the Engineering Team.

What we would love to see from you

In the role of System Integration Senior Engineer ideally, you will have the following:

  • Master’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, or another related field.

  • 5 to 10 years of experience in systems design, analysis, and testing of aerospace or space-related systems, with a focus on integration of complex spacecraft and/or testing activities.

  • Hands-on hardware experience.

  • Practical experience / contact with functional test platforms, such as software in the loop, hardware in the loop, and bench testing.

  • Experience in the development and verification of space hardware.

  • Spacecraft systems knowledge.

Skills and Behaviours

  • Strong oral and written communication skills

  • Strong analysis and problem-solving skills

  • Strong organizing and prioritization of tasks

  • Positive and flexible attitude to get the job done

  • Ability to communicate at all levels of the business

  • Demonstrates behaviors consistent with The Exploration Company’s core values of Mission, Vision, Integrity, Excellence and Teamwork

  • Space enthusiast: ready to change the European space industry

  • Ability to thrive in a high paced development environment

Why you should join us!

What makes us special here at The Exploration Company and why we think you will enjoy working here is:  

  • We’re Agile - we make decisions fast whilst keeping our goals and systems in mind 

  • We’re Open and Collaborative - we are transparent about risks and obstacles, so that we can cooperate to overcome them  

  • We have a lot of Fun - we refuel our energy knowing we are democratising space. It’s a wonderful and rare opportunity, are YOU up for the challenge?

title: Talent Partner, GTM
descriptionHtml:
Talent Partner, GTM

Location: London, onsite 4 days a week.
Duration: 12-month fixed term contract

Retire The ERP.

Light exists to replace factory-era ERPs with software that feels alive. Our Smart Financial Platform gives modern, global companies superpowers: automated accounting, real-time reporting, and financial flows that move at the speed of the business.

We build with our customers, ship fast, and obsess over craft. In a short time, Light has gone from idea to the operating core for leading companies like Lovable, Legora, and Keyshot. People don’t just use Light, they enjoy it.

We’re an early team defining a new software category. Think engineers who love debits and credits, designers who care about reconciliation states, and operators who treat finance as a product. If you’re excited to modernise how the world runs money, one workflow at a time, you’re in the right place.

Backed by world-class investors and advised by industry titans, we’re building category-defining products with the freedom to ship ambitiously and own outcomes.

Come help us make Light the global default for next-gen finance.

The Role

We plan to double the team in 2027. Most companies that grow this fast dilute the talent density that made them good. We won’t.

You’ll hire across GTM: the teams that win our customers and tell the world about Light. One week that might be an enterprise account executive, the next a product marketer or a demand generation lead. You’ll lead Marketing hiring and work alongside our Sales Talent Partner on Sales. It will be fast and at times messy, and you’ll be the person who brings structure to it.

This isn’t a role for someone who wants to sit and screen all day. We want a guardian of the bar: someone who steps back, looks at the whole hiring problem and fixes what’s actually in the way. AI and good process handle the volume. You bring the judgement, and relationships with great people long before we need them.

What You’ll Do

  • Own Marketing hiring end to end, from individual contributors to leadership

  • Work on Sales searches alongside our Sales Talent Partner, including account executives, SDRs and partner sellers

  • Partner with Marketing and Sales leaders from the start: shape the role, challenge the brief, and build the scorecards and calibration that keep the bar high

  • Work out why a search is stalling, whether it’s the brief, comp, location, assessment or the market, and fix it. Sometimes the answer isn’t an external hire at all.

  • Map the markets for the GTM profiles we hire most often and build talent pools, so the pipeline exists before roles open

  • Hire internationally, with visa sponsorship and relocation support, as our GTM team expands into new markets

What Success Looks Like In Your First 6 Months

  • Marketing and Sales leaders bring you in early because you make their hiring decisions better

  • Hiring managers know what they’re getting and when, because you’ve told them, with data

  • We have mapped markets and warm talent pools for our most common Marketing and Sales profiles

  • Hires are closing at pace, and every one makes the team stronger

  • At least one AI workflow you’ve built is part of how the whole team works

How Our Talent Team Works

  • We protect talent density. Every hire should raise the average. We’d rather hold a role open a little longer than fill it with the wrong person.

  • We source proactively. Most of our best hires won’t apply, so we don’t wait for a role to open. We map the market, build relationships early and have a pipeline ready when the need arrives.

  • We use data. We know where candidates come from, where they drop out and what predicts a good hire. We use that to challenge hiring managers with evidence.

  • We build with AI. We don’t mean writing job ads with ChatGPT. We mean sourcing workflows, research agents and automations that change how much a recruiter can get done.

What You’ll Get From Us

Most Talent teams are bolting AI onto the way they’ve always worked. We’re building ours AI-first, from the ground up.

  • A team built AI-first. AI does the searching, research and admin, so you can spend your time on judgement, relationships and closing. You’ll help design how that works, rather than having it handed to you.

  • The tools and the time to build. You’ll have Claude, Codex, Lovable, Noon and Ashby from day one, plus a regular team build session to test new workflows. When something works, it becomes how the whole team operates.

  • A strategic role. You’ll help shape GTM hiring plans and market-entry decisions, bringing leadership evidence on where talent sits and what it costs.

  • Real ownership. Marketing hiring is yours to build from the ground up.

What You’ll Bring

  • 4+ years in Talent Acquisition, mostly in-house or in embedded or RPO-style roles, hiring GTM teams, including Marketing, in high-growth B2B SaaS or fintech

  • You switch gears fast. You can move from an enterprise sales search to a product marketing hire in the same afternoon, picking up the language, the market and what good looks like in each.

  • Deep knowledge of the London and European GTM talent market. Without opening LinkedIn, you could tell us which companies build the best Marketing and Sales teams, how they structure comp and OTE, and who’s likely to move.

  • You’re a guardian of the bar. You hold it under pressure, including telling a hiring manager “not this one” when the deadline is tight.

  • You step back before you dive in. When a search isn’t working, your first instinct is to work out why, before you screen more CVs.

  • You work at pace and bring structure to chaos. When priorities shift and reqs pile up, you set a clear plan and keep everyone moving.

  • A track record of proactive sourcing: hires you found and engaged before the role opened, rather than hires that applied

  • Hands-on experience building with AI to improve recruiting, with examples you can walk us through

Bonus Points

  • Hiring GTM teams for new markets

  • Building a Marketing team’s hiring from scratch

  • Experience with Claude, Codex, Lovable, Noon or similar tools

The Good Stuff

🏢 In-office culture, high talent density.
💸 Competitive salary.
🏝 25 days annual leave plus public holidays.
🚀 Shape how Light hires as we double the team.
🥳 Off-sites twice a year. The last 2 were in Tuscany & Provence!

Equal Opportunities

Light is an equal opportunities employer. If you need any adjustments during the hiring process, just let us know.

title: Talent Sourcer
descriptionHtml:
About Us

Tebi is building a modern connected hospitality operating system that helps entrepreneurs run their business more intelligently and smoothly. In one seamless platform, Tebi embeds sales, reservations, kitchen, inventory, and payments (as well as all the data that powers it) helping to automate work, streamline operations, and give hospitality owners the clarity and time they need to focus on what matters the most: creating great guest experiences.

Founded by Arnout Schuijff, co-founder of Adyen, and backed by €50 million in funding from Index Ventures & CapitalG, Tebi is build in service of hospitality first. Thousands of restaurants, cafés, bars, and coffee shops across the Netherlands, UK, Spain, Italy, Denmark, Germany, Finland, and Ireland.

About the Role

You'll be the engine behind our hiring growth. Most of our roles don't fill from applications: great people have to be found, approached and convinced. As our Sourcing Specialist, you'll own the top of our hiring funnel for sales and engineering roles, from the first message to a candidate who's ready to meet the hiring manager.

You'll also own the candidate experience around it: fast replies, smooth scheduling and honest feedback. That's what makes the best people say yes to us. This is a specialist role: we're looking for someone who loves the search and wants to get really good at it. Our recruiters run interviews, offers and closing, so you can stay focused on finding great people.

What You’ll Do

  • Build and run outbound pipelines for sales and engineering roles, especially in cities where Tebi isn't yet known (Munich, Hamburg, Cologne/Düsseldorf, Rome, Milan, Madrid, Barcelona, the Nordics)

  • Write messages that get answers, and follow up without being annoying

  • Run short intro calls and hand promising candidates to our recruiters with a clear summary, not just a profile link

  • Work with our recruiters on the profile for each role: who we want, where they are, what would make them move

  • Own your numbers (messages, replies, intro calls, candidates passed on, hires) and share them weekly

  • Look after the candidates you source: answer quickly, and give honest feedback to those who don’t move forward after the intro call

  • Keep Ashby clean and your hiring data trustworthy: every candidate tracked, every rejection reason filled in.

  • Spot what's slowing our process down and fix it, or tell us what to change

What You’ll Need

  • 3-5 years in sourcing or recruiting, agency or in-house, with real outbound experience

  • A track record of finding people who weren't looking, with examples of roles you filled that way

  • Comfort with Boolean search, LinkedIn Recruiter and Ashby

  • Clear, direct writing and a good phone manner

  • Reliable and organised: you don't let a candidate wait for a reply

  • Curiosity about AI tools and how they can make sourcing faster and better

  • Fluent in English. Dutch or other EU languages are a are a plus

People who succeed at Tebi are independent, curious and passionate about hospitality. If this speaks to you we can be the right fit. Learn more about how we work from our Recipe here: https://www.tebi.com/gb/careers.

Benefits:

  • Start-up equity

  • Competitive salary

  • Lunch in the office

  • Flexible time off

  • Team events

What is Restaurant Software?

Restaurants and other merchants use various software systems such as Point of Sale (POS), Reservations, Kitchen Display Systems (KDS), Payments, Inventory, Staffing, and the list goes on. These systems all need to speak to each other which they frequently don’t. It’s a mess, and we are fixing it.

From buying a croissant at a cafe to having dinner with friends, it’s a €4 Trillion+ global market and a critical part of everyday life in today's economy.

How we use AI at Tebi

We use AI the way our merchants use Tebi, to cut out the friction and get to what matters faster. We believe in a world where AI increases quality, efficiency and speed.

title: Teamleider Electromagnetic Warfare (m/v/x)
descriptionHtml:
Ben jij die ambitieuze Teamleider / R&D engineer die graag helpt om civiele en militaire vliegtuigen veilig, duurzaam en competitief te laten vliegen? Wil jij jezelf verder ontwikkelen en word je enthousiast van techniek, innovatie en duurzaamheid? Wij zijn op zoek naar een teamleider voor de afdeling.

Wat ga je doen?

In een wereld waarin lucht- en ruimtevaartsystemen steeds complexer worden, is het belangrijk om innovatieve oplossingen te ontwikkelen om de veiligheid en efficiëntie te garanderen. Binnen NLR werken we aan de ontwikkeling van geavanceerde aerospace systemen. We maken hierbij gebruik van software modelering en simulatie om het gedrag van complexe systemen te begrijpen en te optimaliseren.

Onze expertise in hardware testen en operationele ondersteuning (OPS) zorgt ervoor dat onze oplossingen niet alleen theoretisch solide zijn, maar ook praktisch toepasbaar en robuust.

De belangstelling voor Electromagnetic Warfare (EW) neemt toe, met de noodzaak om onze lucht- en ruimtevaartsystemen te beschermen tegen elektromagnetische bedreigingen. We zoeken hierom een teamleider binnen onze nieuwe afdeling Aerospace Systems Electronic Warfare (ASEW)

Als teamleider EW zal je leiding geven aan een team van professionals met expertise in het ontwerp, de ontwikkeling en het testen van aerospace systemen met focus op Electronic Warfare.

Binnen onze nieuwe afdeling Aerospace Systems Electromagnetic Warfare zoeken wij een ervaren en gedreven Teamleider om ons team te leiden en te inspireren. De afdeling is gericht op het ontwikkelen van innovatieve oplossingen voor Electromagnetic Warfare (EW) en heeft als doel om de Nederlandse en internationale lucht- en ruimtevaartindustrie te ondersteunen.

Als Teamleider binnen onze afdeling ASEW ben je verantwoordelijk voor het leiden en ontwikkelen van een team van specialisten op het gebied van EW. Je werkt nauw samen met de Afdelingsmanager en andere teams binnen NLR om onze doelen te bereiken.

In afstemming met de Afdelingsmanager ASEW zal je één van de twee Electromagnetic Warfare kennisgebied overzien, namelijk Electronic Warfare Modelling and Simulation of Electronic Warfare Analyses.

In de rol van teamleider blijf je actief en inhoudelijk betrokken bij het uitvoeren van projecten en krijg je de coördinatie over een team van technische collega’s en het verder ontwikkelen en uitbouwen van de faciliteiten waarvoor ASEW verantwoordelijk is. Je bent dus zowel een teamleider als een R&D Engineer.

Als teamleider …

Als teamleider bied jij het team alles wat nodig is om de werkzaamheden van jouw team succesvol te laten verlopen. Je bent de directe leidinggevende van betreffende collega’s en draagt ook de HR-verantwoordelijkheid. Je coacht, stuurt, geeft én vraagt feedback en je pakt de leiding wanneer nodig.

Je stelt hen op deze wijze in staat om optimaal aan de projecten te werken en faciliteer jij hen waar nodig. Je zorgt voor het versterken van de kennispositie van het werkgebied en de realisatie van de werkzaamheden/opdrachten voor interne en externe stakeholders.

Je hebt een open en enthousiasmerende stijl van leidinggeven. Je collega’s voelen zich vrij en gesteund en kunnen zichzelf goed ontwikkelen. Er wordt een goede teamspirit ervaren. Je zorgt voor een goede aansluiting van het werkgebied bij de rest van ASEW en voor het zoeken van synergie met andere afdelingen binnen flight test en certificatie. Je versterkt de samenwerkingsrelaties gericht op het verder volwassen laten worden van het team.

Als R&D Engineer…

Als R&D engineer EW werk je mee aan het veiliger, duurzamer en competitiever maken van de militaire en civiele luchtvaart. Je werkt aan vliegtuigen, helikopters en onbemande vliegende systemen.

Je ondersteunt onze binnen- en buitenlandse opdrachtgevers bij het bereiken van hun doelen. Je voert testen uit, genereerd modellen en analyseert resultaten.

In de rol van R&D engineer, trek of draag je inhoudelijk bij aan projectvoorstellen voor bijvoorbeeld betaalde projecten in opdracht van een (externe) stakeholder. Dit kunnen ook onderzoeksvoorstellen zijn voor bijvoorbeeld defensie onderzoeks-calls.

Verantwoordelijkheden

  • Leiden en ontwikkelen van een team van specialisten op het gebied van EW;

  • Samenwerken met de Afdelingsmanager ASEW en andere teams binnen NLR om onze doelen te bereiken;

  • Overzien van een kennisgebied (Electronic Warfare Modelling and Simulation of Electronic Warfare Analyses) waarmee je samen met de Afdelingsmanager tot strategische doelen van het team komt;

  • Inspireren en motiveren van teamleden om hun beste werk te leveren;

  • Coördineren van projecten en activiteiten om de doelen van de afdeling te bereiken.

Wat breng je mee?

  • Een afgeronde WO master in een relevante discipline (bijv. lucht- en ruimtevaarttechniek, elektrotechniek, informatica);

  • Tenminste 3 jaar ervaring in een leidinggevende functie, bij voorkeur in de lucht- en ruimtevaartindustrie;

  • Aantoonbare kennis en ervaring op het gebied van EW;

  • Uitstekende communicatieve vaardigheden in zowel het Nederlands als het Engels (tenminste op C1 niveau);

  • Sterke leiderschaps- en coachingsvaardigheden;

  • In staat om een team te inspireren en te motiveren om hun beste werk te leveren.

Wat bieden wij jou?

Werken bij NLR, betekent werken in een nationale en internationale hightech omgeving. Samenwerken en betrokkenheid staan bij ons hoog in vaandel. Door jou vrijheid en eigen verantwoordelijkheid te geven, ben jij het best in staat om tot baanbrekende innovaties te komen. Wil jij jezelf vakinhoudelijk én op persoonlijk vlak ontwikkelen? Ook dat kan bij NLR als lerende organisatie, met daarnaast een opleidingsbudget, een mentor, interne coaches en goede contacten met mbo’s, hbo’s en universiteiten.

Naast dit alles bieden wij jou:

  • De kans om bij te dragen aan complexe en maatschappelijk relevante vraagstukken;

  • Voldoende vakantie- en ATV-dagen (in totaal 45 bij fulltime dienstverband) voor een goede werk-privébalans;

  • Een eindejaarsuitkering van 8%;

  • Een tegemoetkoming in jouw zorgkosten;

  • Extra betaald ouderschapsverlof;

  • De mogelijkheid om jezelf te ontwikkelen met opleidingen en cursussen die passen bij jouw ambities.

Jouw nieuwe werkomgeving

Electromagnetic Warfare is een nieuwe afdeling binnen Aerospace systems en is voort gekomen uit de afdeling Defence Operations. Je zult de leidinggevende zijn van een team enthousiaste en gedreven professionals. Hierbij zul je nauw samenwerken met andere NLR afdelingen, in het bijzonder de afdeling waaruit ASEW voortgekomen is. De werkzaamheden zijn direct gerelateerd aan Defensie, weerbaarheid en de verdediging van Nederland en de Nederlandse krijgsmacht.

Je werkt vanuit onze locatie in Amsterdam en zult veel contact met collega's en partners binnen en buiten NLR.

Wat betekent werken bij NLR?

Koninklijke NLR is al ruim 100 jaar een kennisorganisatie met de wil en ambitie om te vernieuwen. Vanuit die drijfveer maken wij de wereld van lucht- en ruimtevaart veiliger, duurzamer, efficiënter en effectiever en staan wij voor baanbrekende innovaties.

Bij ons werken meer dan 1000 gedreven professionals, van vliegtuigbouwkundigen tot psychologen en van wiskundigen tot applicatiedeskundigen. NLR staat voor een inclusieve en diverse organisatie waar iedereen zich welkom, veilig, gewaardeerd en gerespecteerd voelt.

Wil jij meer weten?


Bel of mail dan met Frank Bax (recruiter) via 0615676915 of .

Onze collega’s vertellen jou graag hoe het is om bij NLR te werken. Vergeet trouwens ook niet eens een kijkje op onze socials te nemen zoals ons YouTube kanaal.

Solliciteren?

Mooi, we zijn benieuwd naar jou! Stuur je motivatiebrief en CV via de ‘Solliciteren’ button.

De teamleider is een parttime functie.

Een assessment maakt deel uit van de procedure.

Een positieve uitkomst van een veiligheidsonderzoek (VGB) is een voorwaarde voor indiensttreding. Meer informatie daarover lees je op de website van de MIVD.

Acquisitie wordt niet op prijs gesteld!

title: Teamleitung Naturnaher Wasserbau / Gewässerentwicklung (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
Hier machst du dein Ding. Und wenn es passt, wird es auch deins.

Du planst Renaturierungen, Hochwasserschutz, Gewässerentwicklung. Fachlich macht dir so schnell keiner was vor. Was oft fehlt, ist der Raum dafür: Über dein Projekt entscheidet am Ende jemand, der nie am Gewässer stand, dein Budget verantwortest du nur auf dem Papier, und mit dem Kunden spricht jemand anderes.

Selbst wirksam werden. Bei Stowasserplan führst du dein eigenes Team, steuerst deinen Bereich wirtschaftlich und sprichst selbst mit deinen Auftraggebern. Du entscheidest, wie ihr arbeitet, und siehst direkt, was deine Entscheidungen bewirken. Nicht weil wir die besseren Ingenieure wären, sondern weil wir kurze Wege haben.

Schrittweise einsteigen. Wir suchen keine Führungskraft auf Zeit. Wer sich bei uns gut anstellt, unternehmerisch denkt und Verantwortung übernehmen will, kann sich nach einer Einarbeitungs- und Bewährungsphase am Unternehmen beteiligen und diese Beteiligung Schritt für Schritt ausbauen. So profitierst du direkt von dem Wert, den du mit deinem Team schaffst. Bei uns führt ein Weg von der Teamleitung zur Mitgesellschafterin oder zum Mitgesellschafter.

Wer wir sind

Stowasserplan plant seit 2009 naturnahen Wasserbau: Renaturierung von Fließgewässern, nachhaltiger Hochwasserschutz, Starkregen- und Erosionsvorsorge, Revitalisierung von Auen. Ingenieurbiologische Bauweisen sind unsere Kernkompetenz, nicht ein Zusatz im Leistungsverzeichnis.

Wie das aussieht, wenn es gelingt: Am renaturierten Pleißenbach spielen heute Kinder am Wasser. Am Hoyerswerdaer Schwarzwasser ist der Eisvogel zurück. Von der Machbarkeitsstudie über die Objektplanung nach HOAI bis zur Umweltbaubegleitung machen wir das komplett selbst.

Mit unserem Schwesterunternehmen Stowasserservice entwickeln wir aus unserer Praxiserfahrung Software, mit der andere Büros und Verwaltungen arbeiten: PROGEMIS für das Gewässermanagement, SOFIE für die Ingenieurbiologie. KI nutzen wir zunehmend als Werkzeug in unseren Planungsabläufen. Die fachliche Verantwortung bleibt beim Menschen.

Was du übernimmst

  • Ein Team von fünf bis acht Leuten: Projektverantwortliche, Projektmitarbeitende, Praktikanten. Du führst sie, planst Kapazitäten, führst die Mitarbeitergespräche und arbeitest neue Leute ein.
  • Die wirtschaftliche Steuerung deines Bereichs: Budgets, Termine, Qualität, Nachträge. Nach der Einarbeitung entscheidest du im vereinbarten Rahmen ohne Rücksprache.
  • Die Kundenbeziehung. Du sprichst selbst mit den Gewässerverantwortlichen in Städten und Verbänden, schreibst Angebote, verhandelst und holst Folgeaufträge.
  • Der Teil, für den uns heute die Zeit fehlt: KI-gestütztes Arbeiten in Prozesse einbauen, die halten. Projektstandards, Vorlagen, Qualitätssicherung, Wer das kann, prägt hier die nächsten Jahre.

Was du mitbringst

  • Führungserfahrung. Du hast mehrere Jahre eigenständig Projekte in Flussbau, Ingenieurbau, Wasserwirtschaft oder Regenwassermanagement geleitet und dabei Verantwortung für Menschen übernommen. Du weißt, wie man Aufgaben verteilt, Menschen entwickelt, Konflikte klärt und Entscheidungen auch dann trägt, wenn sie unbequem sind.
  • Du führst gern. Es macht dir Spaß, wenn dein Team besser wird, nicht nur, wenn dein Projekt gut läuft. Gespräche mit deinen Leuten siehst du als Teil deiner Arbeit, nicht als Unterbrechung. Begeisterte Kunden sind dein Maßstab.
  • Ein Studium im Bereich Bauingenieurwesen / Wasserbau, Landschaftsarchitektur, Umwelt- oder Landschaftsplanung oder etwas Vergleichbares.
  • HOAI sitzt, Baustelle ist dir vertraut, und im Vergaberecht (VgV, UVgO, VOB/A) kennst du dich sicher aus, als Bieter wie bei der Vorbereitung von Bauvergaben.
  • Praktische KI-Erfahrung. Du nutzt KI-Werkzeuge bereits im Arbeitsalltag, etwa für Recherche, Texte, Auswertungen oder Angebote, kennst ihre Grenzen und hast Lust, das mit deinem Team weiterzuentwickeln.

Naturnahen Wasserbau und Ingenieurbiologie musst du nicht mitbringen. Das ist unser Kernwissen, und wir bringen es dir bei. Dafür nehmen wir uns Zeit und planen es ein.

Was du bekommst

  • Entscheidungen, die du triffst, statt Entscheidungen, die du vorbereitest.
  • 60.000 bis 70.000 Euro, je nach Erfahrung.
  • Flexible Arbeitszeiten und die Möglichkeit, an ein bis zwei Tagen pro Woche im Homeoffice zu arbeiten.
  • Fortbildung, die wir bezahlen und für die du Arbeitszeit bekommst.
  • Ein Büro, das wächst. Wir gehen in die DACH-Region. Das schafft Aufgaben, die es heute noch nicht gibt.
  • Eine unternehmerische Perspektive: Wenn die Zusammenarbeit trägt, kannst du dich schrittweise am Unternehmen beteiligen.

Warum es diese Stelle gibt

Wir wachsen. Dafür bauen wir unseren Führungskreis aus und besetzen eine weitere Teamleitung in Vollzeit.

Du kommst nicht in ein fertiges Team, sondern in eines, das gerade neu sortiert und erweitert wird. Wer darin die Chance sieht, ist hier richtig.

title: Tech Lead - Go & React
descriptionHtml:
• Role Title: Tech Lead
    Department: Engineering

    Role Summary
    As a Tech Lead at CreateFuture, you will use your technical and leadership skills to lead
    and support diverse client projects. Depending on the engagement, this includes
    hands-on coding, software architecture, solution design or delivery leadership and project
    management, ensuring a high standard of delivery in everything we do.
    We focus on high-value, high-impact client outcomes, and we’re not afraid to challenge
    the status quo. You should be curious, pragmatic, and operate well in ambiguous
    environments.
    As a technology consultancy, it’s important for us to not only deliver reliable, scalable
    solutions but to be looking at future trends and other high-impact developments. Your
    curiosity for technology and its application to business opportunities is highly valued
    within the company. We are disrupting consultancy through the use of Artificial
    Intelligence and radical thinking in our approach. We're doing something different, and
    that’s realising significant benefits for our clients. We want you to share that same
    ambition.
    You will also manage a team of technical direct reports, who are themselves working on
    client projects, for whom you will provide actionable feedback, technical guidance and
    mentoring, fostering a continuous improvement, growth and consultancy mindset.
    You will work with clients at every level to understand their problems, set expectations,
    and maximise business value, representing CreateFuture as an engagement lead.
    Role Requirements
    ● Proven, hands-on technical leader delivering complex software.
    ● Demonstrate thought-leadership; supporting our clients and colleagues to
    understand, through modern technology and process, what is possible for their
    business/craft.
    ● Line-manage a team of engineers while maintaining personal delivery
    contributions.
    ● Commercial experience in at least one: Java, .NET, Python, or TypeScript (backend
    or frontend).

    ● Commercial experience with at least one major cloud (Amazon Web Services,
    Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud Platform) and modern infrastructure practices
    (containers, continuous integration/continuous delivery, infrastructure as code).
    ● Strong delivery fundamentals: estimation, planning, and risk/issue/dependency
    management; escalates early with clear options and impacts.
    ● Communicate designs and trade-offs clearly to technical and non-technical
    stakeholders.
    ● Skilled in difficult conversations and actionable feedback; sets clear standards and
    holds people accountable.
    Desirable:
    ● Tailor ways of working (Scrum or Kanban) to context and drive continuous
    improvement.
    ● Experience in change transformation projects that involved significant Artificial
    Intelligence adoption.
    ● Breadth across multiple languages or disciplines (e.g., Rust, test automation,
    DevOps/platform engineering).
    ● Experience across multiple clouds and cloud-native services.
    ● Contribute to recruitment and pre-sales in a consultancy context.
    ● Represent CreateFuture in the external tech community.
    Role Responsibilities
    Technical leadership:
    ● Communicate designs, trade‐offs, and constraints in the context of client goals.
    ● Lead architecture, solution design, and documentation; make pragmatic
    technology choices.
    ● Contribute code where appropriate; set engineering standards; ensure reviews,
    testing, and maintainability.
    ● Troubleshoot complex issues; drive root‐cause fixes and follow‐up actions.
    Delivery leadership:
    ● Own technical outcomes: scope, estimate, plan, and track to agreed goals.
    ● Highlight risks, issues, and dependencies; escalate early with clear options,
    impacts, and recommendations.
    ● Ensure actionable backlogs and realistic plans; communicate timelines and team
    shape needs.
    People leadership (enable, unblock, hold to account):

    ● Guide direct reports to set themselves clear personal goals, and hold them
    accountable for realising them.
    ● Proactively remove impediments across technical, process, and organisational
    boundaries.
    ● Hold colleagues accountable for commitments and standards; address
    performance issues promptly.
    ● Provide targeted guidance and feedback; recognise achievements.
    ● Line‐manage direct reports; run core rituals (team meetings, 1:1s, objectives,
    reviews).
    ● Contribute to hiring.
    Client leadership:
    ● Build trusted relationships at all levels; translate business needs into technical
    plans.
    ● Manage expectations and scope; articulate value and trade‐offs; identify follow‐on
    opportunities.
    ● Represent CreateFuture as the engagement lead.
    Optional/community:
    ● Contribute to delivery practices and standards
    ● Contribute to pre‐sales.

What we’ll offer you:

We trust people to do their best work. That means flexibility over rigid rules, impact over activity, and real investment in your growth both professionally and personally. You’ll be part of a supportive, and friendly culture, surrounded by smart, curious people who care deeply about what they do.

We offer flexible working, including hybrid and remote options. Our office hubs are located in Edinburgh, Leeds, Manchester, London and Bulgaria, with occasional travel to client sites or CreateFuture offices when needed.

We trust you to manage your time balancing collaboration with client time and focused work. What matters is the impact you have, not how busy you look.

Our hiring process

We try to keep our hiring process clear, fair and respectful of your time. We aim to get back to everyone who applies and we will be upfront about where you are in the process.

It usually looks like this:

  • Call with our Talent Acquisition Team 
  • Role specific capability interview 

Depending on the role, we might also ask you to do a short presentation, a practical or technical task or have a values focused conversation. We will explain what is involved before anything happens.

Inclusion at CreateFuture 

We believe diverse teams build better workplaces and better products. We want CreateFuture to be a place where people feel able to be themselves and do their best work.

If you need any adjustments or support during the application process, just. We will do what we can to help.

We look forward to your application!

descriptionHtml:
About Pelico

Traditional industrial manufacturing systems were built for predictability. Supply chains no longer are. Today, real-time data is buried in legacy tools that weren't designed for constant disruption. By the time an issue surfaces, it has already snowballed, sending everyone into firefighting mode. Pelico exists to close the gap between production plans and the daily reality on the factory floor.

We've built the manufacturing orchestration platform trusted by the world's most complex industrial operations : companies like Airbus, Boeing, Safran, Eaton, and Cartier. Our AI connects fragmented supply chain, production, and quality data into a single live operational picture — then puts AI agents to work anticipating disruptions, simulating recovery options, and keeping every team aligned before small problems become expensive ones.

Founded in 2019 and backed by General Catalyst, 83North, and Serena, we've raised $72M and are growing fast — 300% year-over-year revenue growth, deployed in 15+ countries, and supporting factories worldwide. We're headquartered in Paris, with offices in Miami, London and Amsterdam, and we're just getting started.

This is a rare chance to join a company that's redefining an industry that hasn't been disrupted in decades — from the inside.

About the Platform squads

Pelico is a configuration-driven, AI-native platform: a field engineer stands up a running factory application by authoring YAML — schema, algorithms, widgets, actions, agents — instead of writing code. The Platform squads build the reusable blocks that make that possible, and we run them as a product: our customers are other engineers — the Solution squads, our Regional Solution Engineering pods, and customer AI teams building on top of us.

You'll lead one squad — the configurability framework, the compute layer, the widget surface, the agent-development substrate (MCP/LSP/harness/BYOM), the integration layer, or the end-user Copilot — owning a capability cluster the whole company builds on.

Your mission

You'll own a platform capability end to end — and ship it yourself:

  1. Build the substrate. Author the framework, SPI, runtime, or AI tooling other squads depend on, and review the rest at architectural depth.

  2. Run it as a product. Own the roadmap, the contracts your consumers rely on, the adoption metric, and the deprecation policy that keeps the surface clean.

  3. Set the bar. Author specs, run the spec-driven workflow, and stand up the eval and review gates that make agent-authored code trustworthy.

  4. Harvest the field. Turn recurring customer patterns into platform capabilities, so learning compounds instead of fragmenting into bespoke forks.

  5. Lead by example. Write the load-bearing code, pair with your engineers, raise their craft, and grow the squad as the leverage you ship earns it.

Your impact

Every Solution squad and every customer deployment is only as strong as the platform underneath it. Own a capability cluster well and you create leverage the entire company compounds on — the difference between a platform that scales and a pile of one-off forks.

What we're looking for

This is a lead-by-example role for a senior engineer who builds platforms other engineers love. You're excited by deep, high-blast-radius problems, you measure yourself by what others build on your work, and you lead by being among the best engineers in the room.

You'll need:

  • A track record of shipping production platform / framework / infrastructure that other engineers build on (SPIs, libraries, runtimes, dev tooling, or AI substrate)

  • Deep, current hands-on coding — we build in Kotlin / Java 25 (TypeScript/React for the experience squads); strong here, or a fast learner

  • Real API / SPI / abstraction-design judgment, with a feel for performance and correctness at scale (up to hundreds of millions of records)

  • A platform-as-product mindset — you optimize for adoption and others' leverage, and you're comfortable deprecating

  • A track record of leading senior engineers by example, not by leaving the keyboard

Nice to have:

  • Running a team as an internal platform (adoption metrics, internal NPS, deprecation, roadmap)

  • Squad-relevant depth — codegen/annotation processors, Kubernetes/IaC/observability, React/design systems, MCP/LSP/agent harnesses, ERP/connectors, or end-user agent UX

  • AI-native ways of working (agentic workflows, eval harnesses, spec-driven development)

  • Aerospace / defense / discrete-manufacturing context

  • French is a plus, not a requirement

If you bring the essentials and a strong mix of the rest, we want to hear from you — we're hiring the person who'll make this real, not a checklist.

What we offer

  • A real ownership mandate over a capability cluster, with equity in a category-defining scale-up

  • Deep, high-leverage problems with real customers and real scale

  • An AI-native engineering culture and a small, elite squad — be challenged, learn, and have fun

  • Hybrid working from our Paris HQ, an international team of 36+ nationalities

Your interview experience

  1. Intro call with Talent Acquisition (30 min)

  2. Hiring manager conversation with the VP Engineering (45 min)

  3. Case Study onsite 1h30 / 2h

  4. Leadership conversation + founders (CEO/CTO)

  5. Offer + References, run in parallel

Pelico is an equal opportunity employer. We're committed to building a diverse team and an inclusive environment where everyone can do their best work.

title: Tech Lead - Shared Backend Services
descriptionHtml:
Tech Lead - Shared Backend Services

Hybrid in London (UK) or Remote within the UK

We’re looking for a Tech Lead to join the Funnel Platform team.

You’ll lead the team behind the shared services and frameworks that iwoca’s engineers build on. Those engineers are your customers, and the shared backend services feed iwoca’s lending decisions.

The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The Team

Funnel Platform takes its name from iwoca’s customer funnel – a business’s journey from first application to repeat lending. It owns the shared services and frameworks that the customer journey teams along that funnel build on, in the UK and Germany. The team’s aim is to make those services reliable, and simple for other teams to change.

The team works across three areas:

  • Credit data. Looking after the services that bring in data from the UK credit bureaus and Companies House.

  • Bank data. Looking after the service other teams use to work with business bank transactions.

  • New shared services. Building services that several teams need, including one for split tests.

The team is small – three backend engineers, including you. Infrastructure, such as Kubernetes and cloud hosting, sits with a separate team, so the work here is software.

The Role

As the Tech Lead in Funnel Platform, you’ll stay hands-on in the code while you lead the team. The team has no product manager, so you’ll decide what it builds, with input on priorities from the leaders of iwoca’s customer journey teams. You’ll report to the head of engineering for the customer journey teams.

  • Ownership. You’ll be accountable for the team’s existing services and the new ones it builds, from design to production.

  • Engineering standards. You’ll shape how the team designs and tests the shared services, and review the changes other teams make to them.

  • Impact. You’ll improve the services iwoca’s customer journey teams depend on, so your work speeds up theirs.

  • Influence. You’ll use data to persuade the customer journey teams and their leaders to back shared-service work that helps all of them.

  • Leadership and growth. You’ll line-manage the team’s two engineers, and give them the guidance and context to lead projects of their own.

The requirements

Essential:

  • Technical leadership. You’ve led engineers as a tech lead for around two years, while staying hands-on in the code.

  • Shared services. You’ve built and run backend services or frameworks that other engineering teams use and contribute to. You’ve reviewed their changes and shaped how they use your work.

  • Backend engineering. You know at least one backend language in depth, and you’ve designed and run distributed systems in production.

  • Problem finding. You’ve set a team’s priorities without a product manager, talking to the people who use your work to find the real problem before you design a fix. You can show what a technical trade-off costs or saves the business.

  • AI leverage. You’ve used AI to produce work you couldn’t have delivered without it – such as an internal tool or a migration. You know where it helps keep shared code easy to maintain, and you review what it produces before it goes live.

Bonus:

  • Python and Django. You’ve built production services in Python with Django.

  • Numerical background. You’re comfortable analysing data and drawing conclusions you can defend.

  • Experimentation. You’ve built tools that other teams use to run split tests.

  • Fintech. You’ve worked at a fintech or another financial services business.

The salary

We expect to pay from £100,000 to £130,000 for this role. But, we’re open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

The culture

At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.

We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them.

The offices

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

  • Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits

  • Flexible working hours.

  • Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

  • A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

  • 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

  • A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

  • Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

  • 3% Pension contributions on total earnings.

  • An employee equity incentive scheme.

  • Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

  • Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

  • Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

  • A learning and development budget for everyone.

  • Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.

  • Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

Useful links:

  • iwoca benefits & policies

  • Interview welcome pack

Compensation: £100K – £130K

title: Tech Talent Partner
descriptionHtml:
Our Mission
Human time and effort is the rarest thing in the universe. The fact that so many people hate what they do for work is a disaster on so many levels. How many people live quiet lives of misery? How many generational talents do we miss due to circumstance?

Dex’s mission is to close the gap between Talent & Opportunity, we believe that work, and being productive, is part of the human condition, that regardless of AI, human passion, ingenuity and a desire to do things means that work will always exist.

We are building Dex to create a future where technology helps every individual to understand their strengths, interests and unique abilities, and to connect with opportunities where they can thrive, because more people doing things they love leads to a better, happier and more productive world.

We are starting by connecting the world's most ambitious software engineers with the companies that deserve them.

Why this role is different

The AI startups and scaleups we work with have roles they can’t fill. Not because they haven’t tried, but because they have world-class hiring bars, and it’s genuinely tough.

As a Talent Partner, you own those client relationships end to end. You take a role brief properly, you push back when it doesn’t add up, and you become the person a founder, internal talent partner or hiring manager calls before they’ve even decided to hire. You also own delivery, making sure every client has an amazing experience using Dex, from brief through to signed offer.

We’re an AI-first company, and our talent team is pushing the boundaries of what AI can do in recruitment. You won’t just be using AI tools, you’ll be part of the team working out what great hiring looks like when AI is built into every step.

You’ll also shape the product. You’ll work directly with our product and engineering teams, who are building tools specifically for you. When something isn’t working, whether it’s a match that shouldn’t have reached you or a workflow that slows you down, you raise it with the people who can fix it, and you see it change. Talent Partners are brought in early on anything that touches their workflow, so you help decide what gets built, not just use it.

What you’ll do

  • Own a portfolio of client relationships end to end: brief, delivery, feedback, and everything after

  • Take role briefs and kick-offs that actually hold up. Scope the role, interrogate the requirements, and tell a client when the role is really two roles, or shouldn’t be hired at all

  • Run the process on the client side: keep feedback fast, keep interviews moving, and keep momentum from breaking

  • Use funnel data to diagnose stalling roles and walk clients through where they’re losing people and why

  • Negotiate and close offers so that neither side feels managed

  • Grow accounts from one search into the whole hiring plan

You’ll probably have

  • 2+ years in tech or engineering recruitment, either in-house at a startup or scaleup or at a specialist tech agency

  • Hired for roles like backend, infra, ML/AI engineers, researchers or founding engineers, and the ability to hold a credible conversation with a CTO about what a role really needs

  • Strong command of funnel metrics: you know what good conversion looks like at each stage and what to do when it isn’t happening

  • Commercial sharpness and the confidence to push back on senior people early, rather than having the expensive conversation late

  • Curiosity about AI tooling. You’ll be a daily power user of a product that’s being built around you

Why join now

You’ll be building relationships with some of the best AI startups and scaleups on the planet, helping them hire the roles they care most about. You’ll have experienced talent leaders around you day to day, and a product team building tools for you specifically. This is a team that deeply understands how difficult and how important hiring is.

We’re open on backgrounds. If you have the raw ingredients and have excelled where you are now, we want to hear from you, even if you don’t tick every box.

What we offer

  • Above market base salary plus uncapped commission; we're building a world class team and believe pay should match that ambition

  • Significant equity - we want this to be the last job you 'have' to take

  • Full private healthcare & dental - because life happens and we want to support you

  • Fertility benefits & enhanced parental support

  • Gym membership & wellness benefits

  • Claude tokens - lots and lots of Claude tokens

  • Regular socials, offsites and an annual trip

  • MacBook Pro + team kit

  • "Whatever you need" approach to tools and support

The process

Our hiring process is designed to be transparent and respectful of your time. Here's what you can expect:

  • Talent Screen: Becca (Head of Talent) 30m

  • Hiring Manager Interview: Richard, who heads up Talent Operations at Dex (30-45m)

  • Short Take Home Exercise

  • Task Review (60m)

  • In person interview

    • Culture Fit & Values (45m)

    • Final Interview with Paddy, CEO and Founder at Dex (30m)

title: Technical Instructional Designer (AI Programmes)
descriptionHtml:
Multiverse is the upskilling platform for AI and Tech adoption.

We have partnered with 1,500+ companies to deliver a new kind of learning that's transforming today’s workforce.

Our upskilling apprenticeships are designed for people of any age and career stage to build critical AI, data, and tech skills. Our learners have driven $2bn+ ROI for their employers, using the skills they’ve learned to improve productivity and measurable performance.

In April 2026, we announced $70 million in strategic funding, led by Schroders Capital, with participation from StepStone Group, Lightspeed Venture Partners and General Catalyst. At an increased valuation of $2.1bn, the round makes us Europe’s first EdTech double unicorn.

But we aren’t stopping there. With a strong operational footprint and 800+ employees, we have ambitious plans to continue scaling. We’re building a world where tech skills unlock people’s potential and output.

Join Multiverse and power our mission to equip the workforce to win in the AI era.

The opportunity

AI can draft a lesson in seconds. It can't tell you whether that lesson will actually land with a nervous career-switcher three weeks into an AI apprenticeship — or whether the concept it just explained is subtly, but fundamentally, flawed.

That's where you come in.

You'll be the human judgement layer sitting on top of our AI-assisted content pipeline — part subject-matter expert, part instructional designer. You'll decide what AI got right, fix what it didn't, and build the parts no AI can: the high-touch, high-stakes, deeply human moments in a learner's journey that make the difference between content that's technically correct and content that actually changes someone's career.

You'll have experience building content in generative and/or agentic AI — not just someone who's read about it, but someone who can explain it, question it, and know when the AI-generated explanation of tricky subjects is actually going to help a learner or quietly confuse them.

 

What you'll actually do

  • Design outcomes, not just content. Apply end-to-end backward design to build AI programmes and content where success is measured by what learners can do on the job — not just what they can pass a test on. You'll own the hardest part: turning a job-aligned outcome into content that actually gets learners there.

  • Chase real-world impact, relentlessly. When a piece of learning isn't landing — when an AI practitioner cohort isn't showing the outcomes it should — you won't wait to be told. You'll spot it, own it, and scope the revisions that bring it up to the standard it needs to hit.

  • Build what AI can't. Design the custom, high-touch programmes and creative assets — branching narratives, bespoke multimedia, high-stakes onboarding moments — that need real human empathy, creativity, and nuance. If AI could have built it, it's not your job; if only a person could, it is.

  • Put AI to work, deliberately. Use AI tools and prompt engineering to accelerate your own content development and uncover learning design approaches nobody's tried yet. This isn't about using AI because it's there — it's about knowing exactly where it earns its place.

  • Advise up, not just build. Work directly with Programme Designers and senior stakeholders on the quality and pedagogical effectiveness of the content you design. Your feedback doesn't stay in the room — it shapes how our rules, principles and frameworks evolve.

  • Prototype for the long game. Lead new learning formats and modalities that don't exist yet — and know how to balance shipping fast against building something sustainable enough to reuse.

     

What you'll bring

  • Real command of end-to-end ADDIE and backward design — you've built measurable, job-aligned outcomes and the assessments that prove learners hit them, not just theoretical frameworks on a CV.

  • A habit of treating "good enough" as a starting point, not a finish line — you notice when learning isn't driving real outcomes, and you take the initiative to fix it.

  • Genuine fluency with AI-powered tools and prompt engineering, used to accelerate content development and find genuinely new applications in learning design.

  • The ability to take a genuinely complex generative and/or agentic AI concept and design a learning experience around it that actually works — for a range of different learner personas

  • The confidence and track record to influence peers and senior stakeholders toward a specific, measurable curriculum improvement — not just raise a concern and move on.

  • Resilience when things don't go to plan — you can point to a time a project hit a real obstacle (a blocker, a shifting SME, a launch that missed the mark) and describe exactly what you did about it, and what you learned.

What gets you in the door

You'll need at least one of these:

  • Hands-on experience producing technical content for generative and/or agentic AI.

  • 2+ years designing instructional content in a commercial environment or for commercial clients.

  • Plus one of:

    • A Data or Computer Science degree (or close cousin of one)

    • Completion of a technical apprenticeship in Data or AI

    • 2+ years working as a practitioner in Data or AI

 

If you're a strong technical practitioner who's never formally studied instructional design, or a seasoned learning designer who's spent the last year deep in AI tools — either path can get you here. We're looking for the judgment, not a checklist.

 

What we'll actually explore together

We're upfront about what our process looks for, because we'd rather you come prepared to talk about the real thing than guess what we want to hear. Across the conversations, we'll dig into:

  • Advanced curriculum & applied design — how you turn an end-to-end backward-design process into measurable, job-aligned outcomes, and how you build creative assets that genuinely need a human touch.

  • Impact & excellence — what you do when a piece of learning isn't hitting its real-world mark, and how you weigh speed against building something built to last.

  • AI integration & innovation — where and how you've put AI tools and prompt engineering to work, and what that's actually unlocked.

  • Influence & stakeholder management — how you've moved a curriculum forward through a genuine disagreement or feedback conversation, not just delivered a good pitch.

  • Coachability & resilience — how you've handled a launch that didn't land, or a project blocker outside your control, and what you changed as a result.

Benefits

  • Time off - 27 days holiday, plus 5 additional days off: 1 life event day, 2 volunteer days, 2 company-wide wellbeing days (M-Powered Weekend) and 8 bank holidays per year

  • Health & Wellness- private medical Insurance with Bupa, a medical cashback scheme, life insurance, gym membership & wellness resources through Wellhub and access to Spill - all in one mental health support

  • Hybrid work offering - for most roles we collaborate in the office three days per week with the exception of Coaches and Instructors who collaborate in the office once a month

  • Work-from-anywhere scheme - you'll have the opportunity to work from anywhere, up to 10 days per year

  • Space to connect: Beyond the desk, we make time for weekly catch-ups, seasonal celebrations, and have a kitchen that’s always stocked!


Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

We’re an equal opportunities employer. And proud of it. Every applicant and employee is afforded the same opportunities regardless of race, colour, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression, or veteran status. This will never change. Read our Equality, Diversity & Inclusion policy here.

Our Commitment to Safeguarding

Multiverse is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of our learners. We expect all employees to share this commitment and adhere to our Safeguarding Policy, our Prevent Policy and all other Multiverse company policies. Successful applicants will be required to undertake at least a Basic check via the Disclosure Barring Service (DBS).

For roles that will involve a Regulated Activity, successful applicants must also undergo an Enhanced DBS check, including a Children’s Barred List check and a Prohibition Order check. Roles involving Regulated Activity may interact with vulnerable groups, therefore are exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 meaning applicants are required to declare any convictions, cautions, reprimands, and final warnings.

Providing false information is an offence and could result in the application being rejected or summary dismissal if the applicant has been selected, and possible referral to the police and the DBS.

title: Technical Pre Sales Engineer (f/m/d)
descriptionHtml:
Founded in 2010, Luware is a leading SaaS provider specializing in innovative contact center and conversation recording solutions. Our Microsoft-certified solutions are designed to streamline customer interactions. We're committed to innovation and growth, fostering a culture that embraces agile methodologies and flexible work arrangements.

We’re growing fast – and we’re hiring!

As a Technical Pre-Sales Engineer, you help customers across Switzerland, France, Italy, Germany and Austria find the right solution fast. You translate their needs into tailored showcases on our platform, whether by selecting, configuring or building them.

Your analytical mindset and creativity will shine as you run POCs with customers, guiding them in designing and validating their technical concept.

We’re looking for a dynamic, personable and communicative team player to join us as soon as possible or by arrangement.

  • A motivating and supportive team culture where your ideas matter
  • Excellent opportunities for personal and professional growth

title: Technical Project Manager - Engineering Delivery
descriptionHtml:
Diabolocom is looking for a Technical Project Manager to coordinate engineering delivery across our organization and work closely with the Head of Software Engineering on roadmap execution.

You will work across Engineering, Product, Infrastructure and Project teams to keep delivery on track, manage dependencies, identify risks early, and help turn delivery challenges into clear actions and decisions.

We are looking for someone with a software engineering background who has moved into technical leadership and genuinely enjoys the operational side of engineering.

The role

Our engineering organization includes around 90 engineers across 12 teams, working on a complex global product and multiple parallel initiatives.

This role combines ownership of our engineering delivery processes with hands-on execution. You will be responsible not only for running these processes, but also for continuously improving how we plan, coordinate and track delivery across the organization.

Process ownership

You will own and continuously improve:

  • engineering delivery planning processes
  • delivery tracking and reporting
  • cross-team coordination and dependency management.

You will build on our existing practices and ClickUp workflows, identifying what can work better and evolving the processes as the organization and product develop.

Delivery execution

Day to day, you will:

  • track delivery across teams and releases
  • coordinate dependencies and clarify ownership across teams
  • identify risks, blockers and delivery gaps early
  • challenge unclear timelines, priorities and commitments
  • coordinate next steps when delivery is at risk
  • provide clear visibility on delivery status and progress.

You will work closely with Engineering, Product, Infrastructure and Project teams to facilitate alignment.

The objective is simple: make software delivery predictable, transparent and effective.

What success looks like

First few weeks: You start taking ownership of delivery operations and become effective in coordinating ongoing delivery.

Within ~6-8 weeks: You understand the roadmap, teams, dependencies and delivery processes well enough to manage them confidently and start identifying opportunities for improvement.

Within 3 months: You operate autonomously across day-to-day engineering delivery coordination, bringing in the Head of Software Engineering when decisions or trade-offs require escalation.

Your work will directly influence our delivery efficiency and predictability: how much we can take on and how reliably we deliver what we commit to.

Who we are looking for

We are looking for someone who started in software engineering and moved into technical leadership, for example, an Engineering Manager, Technical Lead, senior Team Lead, or Technical Program Manager.

Titles matter less than scope. You need enough technical depth to understand architecture and dependencies, ask the right questions, and navigate complex delivery problems across teams.

We expect

  • around 10 years of experience in software engineering environments
  • at least 3 years in engineering or technical leadership
  • previous hands-on experience as a software engineer
  • experience leading or coordinating multiple engineering teams
  • a track record of delivering complex software initiatives and improving execution
  • strong understanding of the software development lifecycle, distributed systems and cross-team dependencies
  • understanding of Product Management fundamentals
  • experience with Agile and structured project management frameworks such as PMBOK or similar
  • strong prioritization, decision-making and communication skills
  • professional fluency in English.

French and Russian are nice to have.

This role will suit you if…

You still enjoy technical complexity, but what really motivates you is making execution work.

You like finding out why something is stuck and fixing it.

You genuinely enjoy the operational side of engineering: creating structure, improving processes, coordinating teams and making sure things get delivered.

You don’t just want to follow an established process. You naturally look for ways to make it work better.

You are comfortable working across multiple teams, asking difficult questions when needed, and bringing structure to situations where priorities, dependencies or timelines are not immediately clear.

Why Diabolocom

Diabolocom is building one of Europe’s most advanced AI-native CCaaS platforms, powering business-critical customer interactions for 400+ enterprise and mid-market customers across 60+ countries.

We combine a mature global CCaaS platform with a rapidly growing AI Product Suite, backed by our internal AI Research Lab and proprietary AI innovation.

Our ambition goes beyond adding AI features to an existing product. We are building toward a platform capable of orchestrating AI agents, human agents, business workflows and communication channels, with CCaaS as the execution layer.

For Engineering, this means working on the technical and operational challenges of an established enterprise product, from real-time communications and distributed systems to complex integrations, while contributing to its next generation.

With teams across Europe, the US, Brazil and the UAE, and an engineering organization of around 90 people, this role offers the opportunity to work on engineering delivery behind a global product used for critical customer operations.

Why this role

This is a hands-on role combining delivery execution with process ownership.

You will work with the Head of Software Engineering, Team Leads, Product, Infrastructure and Project teams, with a broad view of engineering delivery across the organization.

You will inherit established delivery practices, own them, and continuously improve how we plan, coordinate and track execution.

Recruitment process

  1. Introductory call with Talent Acquisition
  2. Interview with the Head of Software Engineering
  3. Interview with the CTO
  4. Interview with the Head of Product

Logistics

📍 Paris, France
🏢 Hybrid model: minimum 3 days/week onsite
💻 Equipment: choose your preferred setup (Mac/Linux + monitors)
🍽 Lunch vouchers
🚇 Navigo: 50% of the monthly pass reimbursed
🏠 Relocation support available
